title.zh: 卷三百十三 列傳第七十二 富弼 文彥博
title.en: Volume 313 Biographies 72: Fu Bi, Wen Yanbo
title.raw: 卷三百十三 列傳第七十二 富弼 文彥博 Volume 313 Biographies 72: Fu Bi, Wen Yanbo

sentences.zh: 富弼，字彥國，河南人。

translations.literal: Fu Bi, styled Yanguo, was a man of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Bi, whose style name was Yanguo, came from Henan.

sentences.zh: 初，母韓有娠，夢旌旗鶴雁降其庭，云有天赦，已而生弼。

translations.literal: Early on, when his mother the Lady Han was pregnant, she dreamed that banners, cranes, and wild geese descended into her courtyard, and a voice said there would be a heavenly amnesty; thereafter Bi was born.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother Lady Han was still pregnant with him, she dreamed that standards, cranes, and wild geese alighted in her courtyard and a voice announced a heavenly amnesty; soon afterward Bi was born.

sentences.zh: 少篤學，有大度，范仲淹見而奇之，曰：「王佐才也。」

translations.literal: In youth he studied earnestly and had great breadth of mind. Fan Zhongyan saw him and marveled at him, saying: "This is talent fit to assist a king."
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he studied with deep devotion and showed uncommon breadth of character. When Fan Zhongyan met him he was struck with wonder and said, "Here is a man with the makings of a king's right hand."

sentences.zh: 以其文示王曾、晏殊，殊妻以女。

translations.literal: He showed his writings to Wang Zeng and Yan Shu; Shu gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: He had his essays shown to Wang Zeng and Yan Shu, and Shu married his daughter to him.

sentences.zh: 元昊寇鄜延，破金明，鈐轄盧守懃不救，內侍黃德和引兵走，大將劉平戰死，德和誣其降賊。

translations.literal: Yuanhao raided Fuyan, captured Jinming, the supervisory commissioner Lu Shouqin did not rescue it, the inner attendant Huang Dehe led his troops in flight, the great general Liu Ping died in battle, and Dehe falsely accused him of surrendering to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanhao invaded Fuyan and took Jinming, Supervisory Commissioner Lu Shouqin failed to relieve the post, Palace Attendant Huang Dehe fled with his troops, and Major General Liu Ping was killed in battle—after which Dehe slandered Liu as having gone over to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 弼請按竟其獄，德和坐要斬。

translations.literal: Bi requested that the case be fully investigated, and Dehe was sentenced to decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Bi asked that the matter be prosecuted to the end; Dehe was condemned to execution.

sentences.zh: 夏守贇為陝西都部署，又以入內都知王守忠為鈐轄，弼言：「用守贇既為天下笑，今益以守忠，殆與唐監軍無異。

translations.literal: Xia Shouyun was made overall deployment commissioner of Shaanxi, and again the Inner Palace Director Wang Shouzhong was made supervisory commissioner. Bi said: "Employing Shouyun has already made the empire laugh; now to add Shouzhong is scarcely different from the Tang practice of military supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Shouyun was appointed overall deployment commissioner for Shaanxi, and Wang Shouzhong, Director of the Inner Service, was again named supervisory commissioner. Bi said, "Appointing Shouyun has already made the court a laughingstock; to add Shouzhong now is little different from the Tang dynasty's eunuch army supervisors.

sentences.zh: 守懃、德和覆車之轍，可復蹈乎！」

translations.literal: Shouqin and Dehe overturned the cart—can we tread that rut again!"
translations.idiomatic: Shouqin and Dehe have already shown us where that road leads—are we to follow their tracks again?"

sentences.zh: 詔罷守忠。

translations.literal: An edict removed Shouzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Shouzhong dismissed.

sentences.zh: 又請令宰相兼領樞密院。

translations.literal: He also requested that the chief councillors concurrently head the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that the chief ministers take charge of the Bureau of Military Affairs in addition to their civil duties.

sentences.zh: 時西夏首領二人來降，位補借奉職。

translations.literal: At the time two Xi Xia chieftains came to surrender; their ranks were supplemented only with provisional stipendiary posts.
translations.idiomatic: At that time two Tangut leaders defected to the Song, and they were given only provisional stipendiary appointments.

sentences.zh: 弼言當厚賞以勸來者。

translations.literal: Bi said they ought to be richly rewarded to encourage those who would come later.
translations.idiomatic: Bi argued that they should be rewarded generously so as to encourage others to follow.

sentences.zh: 事下中書，宰相初不知也。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the Secretariat, and at first the chief councillors did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter reached the Secretariat, the chief ministers had not even been informed.

sentences.zh: 弼歎曰：「此豈小事，而宰相不知邪！」

translations.literal: Bi sighed and said: "Is this not a small matter—and yet the chief councillors do not know of it!"
translations.idiomatic: Bi sighed and said, "Surely this is no trifle—yet the chief ministers know nothing of it!"

sentences.zh: 更極論之，於是從弼言。

translations.literal: He argued the point to the utmost, and thereupon they followed Bi's advice.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed his argument further, and the court at last adopted his view.

sentences.zh: 除鹽鐵判官、史館修撰，奉使契丹。

translations.literal: He was appointed Salt and Iron Commissioner, Historiographer of the History Office, and sent on embassy to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Salt and Iron Commissioner and reviser at the History Office, and was dispatched as envoy to the Khitan court.

sentences.zh: 慶曆二年，為知制誥，糾察在京刑獄。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qingli he became Drafting Official for the Secretariat and inspector of capital criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingli 2 (1042) he was appointed drafting official for the Secretariat and charged with investigating capital criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 堂吏有偽為僧牒者，開封不敢治。

translations.literal: A hall clerk had forged a monk's certificate, and the Kaifeng authorities did not dare prosecute.
translations.idiomatic: A clerk in the chief ministers' office had forged a Buddhist ordination certificate, and the Kaifeng magistracy did not dare take action.

sentences.zh: 弼白執政，請以吏付獄，呂夷簡不悅。

translations.literal: Bi informed the chief administrators and asked that the clerk be handed over to the courts; Lü Yijian was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Bi reported to the chief administrators and asked that the clerk be handed over for trial; Lü Yijian took offense.

sentences.zh: 會契丹屯兵境上，遣其臣蕭英、劉六符來求關南地。

translations.literal: It happened that the Khitan massed troops on the border and sent their ministers Xiao Ying and Liu Liufu to demand the lands south of the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Khitan stationed troops along the frontier and sent ministers Xiao Ying and Liu Liufu to demand the territory south of the mountain passes.

sentences.zh: 朝廷擇報聘者，皆以其情叵測，莫敢行，夷簡因是薦弼。

translations.literal: The court chose someone to return the embassy, but all regarded their intentions as impossible to fathom and none dared go; Yijian thereupon recommended Bi.
translations.idiomatic: The court sought an envoy to answer the embassy, but everyone judged the Khitan intentions too uncertain to risk the mission, and no one would go—so Yijian recommended Bi.

sentences.zh: 歐陽修引顏真卿使李希烈事，請留之，不報。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu cited Yan Zhenqing's mission to Li Xilie and asked that Bi be kept back; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu cited Yan Zhenqing's fatal embassy to Li Xilie and urged that Bi be kept at home, but the emperor did not reply.

sentences.zh: 弼即入對，叩頭曰：「主憂臣辱，臣不敢愛其死。」

translations.literal: Bi at once entered audience and kowtowed, saying: "When the ruler is troubled the minister is shamed; your servant does not dare spare his life."
translations.idiomatic: Bi went in at once to audience, kowtowed, and said, "When the sovereign is troubled, the minister is disgraced—I dare not cling to my life."

sentences.zh: 帝為動色，先以為接伴。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved in countenance and first appointed him to receive the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's expression changed, and he first named Bi to receive the envoys.

sentences.zh: 英等入境，中使迎勞之，英託疾不拜。

translations.literal: When Ying and the others entered the border, a palace envoy came to welcome and comfort them; Ying pleaded illness and did not bow.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying and his party crossed the border, a palace envoy came out to welcome them, but Ying claimed illness and refused to bow.

sentences.zh: 弼曰：「昔使北，病臥車中，聞命輒起。

translations.literal: Bi said: "When I formerly served as envoy to the north, though ill and lying in the carriage, I rose at once on hearing the command.
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "On my earlier embassy to the north I was sick and lying in my carriage, yet I rose the moment I heard the summons.

sentences.zh: 今中使至而君不拜，何也？」

translations.literal: Now the palace envoy has arrived and you do not bow—why?"
translations.idiomatic: A palace envoy stands before you and you will not bow—why is that?"

sentences.zh: 英矍然起拜。

translations.literal: Ying started up in alarm and bowed.
translations.idiomatic: Ying started in alarm and rose to bow.

sentences.zh: 弼開懷與語，英感悅，亦不復隱其情，遂密以其主所欲得者告曰：「可從，從之；

translations.literal: Bi spoke with him openly and at ease; Ying was moved and pleased and no longer concealed his true intent, and secretly told him what his lord wished to obtain, saying: "You may agree—then agree;
translations.idiomatic: Bi spoke with him candidly; Ying was won over and no longer hid his court's real aims, and confided what his sovereign wanted, saying, "If you can grant it, grant it;

sentences.zh: 不然，以一事塞之足矣。」

translations.literal: if not, blocking them with a single matter will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: if not, fob them off with some other concession and that will be enough."

sentences.zh: 弼具以聞。

translations.literal: Bi reported everything in full.
translations.idiomatic: Bi reported the whole matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝唯許增歲幣，仍以宗室女嫁其子。

translations.literal: The emperor would only permit an increase in the annual tribute and still marry an imperial clanswoman to their ruler's son.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would agree only to raising the annual tribute and to marrying an imperial clanswoman to the Khitan heir.

sentences.zh: 進弼樞密直學士，辭曰：「國家有急，義不憚勞，奈何逆以官爵賂之。」

translations.literal: Bi was advanced to Academician Expositor-in-ordinary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, but he declined, saying: "When the state is in peril, righteousness does not shrink from toil—how can one accept rank and title offered in advance as a bribe?"
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to expositor-academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs, but declined, saying, "When the realm is in crisis, duty does not flinch from hardship—how can I accept rank and title pressed on me beforehand like a bribe?"

sentences.zh: 遂為使報聘。

translations.literal: He then served as envoy on the return embassy.
translations.idiomatic: He then went north as the returning envoy.

sentences.zh: 既至，六符來館客。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Liufu came to lodge him as a guest.
translations.idiomatic: On his arrival Liu Liufu came to receive him as guest.

sentences.zh: 弼見契丹主問故，契丹主曰：「南朝違約，塞雁門，增塘水，治城隍，籍民兵，將以何為？

translations.literal: Bi saw the Khitan ruler and asked the reason; the Khitan ruler said: "The Southern Court has broken the treaty—blocking Yanmen, increasing the frontier ponds, repairing walls and moats, registering militia—what is all this for?
translations.idiomatic: Bi was received by the Khitan emperor and asked the reason for the mission. The emperor said, "The Southern Court has broken faith—closing Yanmen Pass, expanding the border ponds, repairing walls and moats, registering militia—what do you intend by all this?

sentences.zh: 群臣請舉兵而南，吾以謂不若遣使求地，求而不獲，舉兵未晚也。」

translations.literal: My ministers all urge raising troops and marching south; I think it better first to send envoys to demand territory—if the demand is not granted, it will not be too late to take up arms."
translations.idiomatic: My ministers all urge me to march south with an army, but I thought it wiser to send envoys to demand territory first—if that fails, war will not be too late."

sentences.zh: 弼曰：「北朝忘章聖皇帝之大德乎？

translations.literal: Bi said: "Has the Northern Court forgotten the great kindness of Emperor Zhangsheng?
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "Has the Northern Court forgotten the great grace shown by Emperor Zhenzong?

sentences.zh: 澶淵之役，苟從諸將言，北兵無得脫者。

translations.literal: At the Chanyuan campaign, had he followed the generals' counsel, not one northern soldier would have escaped.
translations.idiomatic: At Chanyuan, had he listened to his generals, not a single northern soldier would have returned alive.

sentences.zh: 且北朝與中國通好，則人主專其利，而臣下無獲；

translations.literal: Moreover, when the Northern Court is at peace with China, the ruler alone enjoys the profit and his ministers gain nothing;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when north and south are at peace, the sovereign keeps the profit for himself and his ministers gain nothing;

sentences.zh: 若用兵，則利歸臣下，而人主任其禍。

translations.literal: if arms are used, the profit goes to the ministers and the ruler bears the disaster.
translations.idiomatic: but if war is waged, the profit falls to the ministers while the ruler bears the ruin.

sentences.zh: 故勸用兵者，皆為身謀耳。」

translations.literal: Thus those who urge war are all scheming for themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Those who urge war, then, are all plotting for their own advantage."

sentences.zh: 契丹主驚曰：「何謂也？」

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler was startled and said: "What do you mean?"
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor started and said, "What do you mean by that?"

sentences.zh: 弼曰：「晉高祖欺天叛君，末帝昏亂，土宇狹小，上下離叛，故契丹全師獨克，然壯士健馬物故太半。

translations.literal: Bi said: "Jin Gaozu deceived Heaven and betrayed his lord; the Last Emperor was muddled and chaotic; the realm was narrow and small; high and low were divided in rebellion—therefore the Khitan took the whole army and conquered alone, yet brave men and strong horses perished in more than half.
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "When Gaozu of Jin defied Heaven and betrayed his sovereign, and the last Jin emperor ruled in confusion over a shrunken realm with court and country torn apart, the Khitan could overrun them with a single army—yet even then more than half your brave men and fine horses were lost.

sentences.zh: 今中國提封萬里，精兵百萬，法令修明，上下一心，北朝欲用兵，能保其必勝乎？

translations.literal: Now China extends ten thousand li, has a million crack troops, clear laws and regulations, and unity from top to bottom—if the Northern Court wishes to use arms, can you guarantee certain victory?
translations.idiomatic: Today China spans ten thousand li, fields a million seasoned troops, keeps its laws in good order, and stands united from throne to frontier—if the Northern Court goes to war, can you be sure of victory?

sentences.zh: 就使其勝，所亡士馬，群臣當之歟，抑人主當之歟？

translations.literal: Even supposing victory, of the soldiers and horses lost, will the ministers answer for them, or will the ruler?
translations.idiomatic: Even if you did win, would the ministers pay for the men and horses lost, or would the sovereign?

sentences.zh: 若通好不絕，歲幣盡歸人主，群臣何利焉？」

translations.literal: If friendly relations never cease, the annual tribute all goes to the ruler—what profit is there for the ministers?"
translations.idiomatic: If peace continues, the annual tribute all flows to the throne—what do your ministers gain from that?"

sentences.zh: 契丹主大悟，首肯者久之。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler was greatly enlightened and nodded assent for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor was deeply struck and nodded for a long while in silence.

sentences.zh: 弼又曰：「塞雁門者，以備元昊也。

translations.literal: Bi also said: "Blocking Yanmen is to guard against Yuanhao.
translations.idiomatic: Bi went on, "Yanmen was closed to guard against Yuanhao.

sentences.zh: 塘水始於何承矩，事在通好前。

translations.literal: The frontier ponds began with He Chengjue and antedate the peace.
translations.idiomatic: The border ponds were begun by He Chengjue long before the peace treaty.

sentences.zh: 城隍皆修舊，民兵亦補闕，非違約也。」

translations.literal: The walls and moats are all repairs of old works, and the militia only fill vacancies—this is not breach of treaty."
translations.idiomatic: The walls and moats are only old defenses restored, and the militia rolls merely fill gaps—none of this breaks the treaty."

sentences.zh: 契丹主曰：「微卿言，吾不知其詳。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler said: "But for your words I would not have known the details.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Without your explanation I would never have known the truth of these matters.

sentences.zh: 然所欲得者，祖宗故地耳。

translations.literal: Yet what we wish to obtain is only the ancestral lands.
translations.idiomatic: All we seek, however, is the land of our forefathers.

sentences.zh: 弼曰：「晉以盧龍賂契丹，周世宗復取關南，皆異代事。

translations.literal: Bi said: "Jin ceded Youzhou with Lu-long to bribe the Khitan; Zhou Shizong retook the lands south of the passes—all are affairs of different dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "Jin gave up the Lu-long circuit to buy Khitan favor; Shizong of Zhou retook the southern passes—each belongs to a different age.

sentences.zh: 若各求地，豈北朝之利哉？」

translations.literal: If each dynasty demands territory in turn, how is that to the Northern Court's advantage?"
translations.idiomatic: If every dynasty in turn demanded its old borders back, what advantage would that bring the north?"

sentences.zh: 既退，六符曰：「吾主恥受金帛，堅欲十縣，何如？」

translations.literal: After they withdrew, Liufu said: "Our lord is shamed to receive gold and silk and insists on the ten counties—what of it?"
translations.idiomatic: After they withdrew, Liufu said, "Our sovereign is ashamed to take gold and silk and is set on the ten counties—what say you?"

sentences.zh: 弼曰：「本朝皇帝言，朕為祖宗守國，豈敢妄以土地與人。

translations.literal: Bi said: "Our emperor has said: I guard the realm for my ancestors—how would I dare rashly give land to others?
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "Our emperor has declared, 'I hold this realm for my ancestors—how could I rashly cede territory to another power?

sentences.zh: 北朝所欲，不過租賦爾。

translations.literal: What the Northern Court desires is nothing but rent and tax.
translations.idiomatic: What the north truly wants is nothing but the revenue of those lands.

sentences.zh: 朕不忍多殺兩朝赤子，故屈己增幣以代之。

translations.literal: I cannot bear to slay many innocent subjects of both courts, and therefore humble myself and increase the tribute in place of it.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot bear to see the common people of both courts slaughtered in war, and so I humble myself and increase the annual tribute in their stead.

sentences.zh: 若必欲得地，是志在敗盟，假此為詞耳。

translations.literal: If you must have the land, your aim is to break the alliance and this is only a pretext.
translations.idiomatic: If you insist on taking the land, your aim is to break the treaty and this demand is only a pretext.

sentences.zh: 澶淵之盟，天地鬼神實臨之。

translations.literal: The Chanyuan covenant—Heaven and earth and the spirits truly witnessed it.
translations.idiomatic: The covenant of Chanyuan was witnessed by Heaven, earth, and the spirits.

sentences.zh: 今北朝首發兵端，過不在我。

translations.literal: Now the Northern Court has first raised the banner of war—the fault is not on our side.
translations.idiomatic: Now the north has been first to threaten war—the fault is not ours.

sentences.zh: 天地鬼神，其可欺乎！」

translations.literal: Heaven and earth and the spirits—can they be deceived!"
translations.idiomatic: Heaven, earth, and the spirits—can they be deceived?"

sentences.zh: 明日，契丹主召弼同獵，引弼馬自近，又言得地則歡好可久。

translations.literal: The next day the Khitan ruler summoned Bi to hunt together, drew Bi's horse close to his own, and again said that if land were obtained friendly relations could long endure.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Khitan emperor invited Bi to join a hunt, drew his horse up beside Bi's, and again said that if the land were granted, good relations could last.

sentences.zh: 弼反覆陳必不可狀，且言：「北朝既以得地為榮，南朝必以失地為辱。

translations.literal: Bi repeatedly set forth why it was impossible, and said: "If the Northern Court takes gaining land as glory, the Southern Court must take losing land as shame.
translations.idiomatic: Bi argued again and again that it could not be done, and said, "If the north counts gaining territory as honor, the south must count losing it as disgrace.

sentences.zh: 兄弟之國，豈可使一榮一辱哉？」

translations.literal: As brother states, how can one be honored and the other shamed?"
translations.idiomatic: As brother realms, how can one be honored while the other is humiliated?"

sentences.zh: 獵罷，六符曰：「吾主聞公榮辱之言，意甚感悟。

translations.literal: When the hunt ended, Liufu said: "Our lord heard your words on honor and shame and was deeply moved in mind.
translations.idiomatic: When the hunt ended, Liufu said, "Our sovereign was deeply moved by what you said about honor and shame.

sentences.zh: 今惟有結婚可議耳。」

translations.literal: Now only marriage alliance remains open to discussion."
translations.idiomatic: Now only a marriage alliance remains open to discussion."

sentences.zh: 弼曰：「婚姻易生嫌隙。

translations.literal: Bi said: "Marriage easily breeds suspicion and rifts.
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "Marriage alliances easily breed suspicion and quarrels.

sentences.zh: 本朝長公主出降，齎送不過十萬緡，豈若歲幣無窮之利哉？」

translations.literal: When our court's eldest imperial princess goes down in marriage, the dowry sent does not exceed one hundred thousand strings of cash—how can that compare with the endless profit of annual tribute?"
translations.idiomatic: When an eldest imperial princess of our house is sent in marriage, her dowry never exceeds one hundred thousand strings of cash—how can that match the endless profit of annual tribute?"

sentences.zh: 契丹主諭弼使歸，曰：「俟卿再至，當擇一受之，卿其遂以誓書來。」

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler instructed Bi to return and said: "When you come again, we shall choose one and accept it—bring the oath document accordingly."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor told Bi to return home and said, "When you come again we shall choose one option and accept it—bring the treaty text with you then."

sentences.zh: 弼歸覆命，復持二議及受口傳之詞於政府以往。

translations.literal: Bi returned to report his mission and again took the two proposals and the wording received by oral transmission to the government before proceeding.
translations.idiomatic: Bi returned to report and again carried the two proposals and the orally transmitted terms to the government before setting out once more.

sentences.zh: 行次樂壽，謂副使張茂實曰：「吾為使者而不見國書，脫書詞與口傳異，吾事敗矣。」

translations.literal: Stopping at Leshou, he said to Vice-envoy Zhang Maoshi: "I am envoy yet have not seen the state letter—if the letter's wording differs from the oral transmission, my mission is ruined."
translations.idiomatic: At Leshou he said to Vice-envoy Zhang Maoshi, "I am the chief envoy yet I have not seen the state letter—if its wording differs from what was orally agreed, my mission is ruined."

sentences.zh: 啟視果不同，即馳還都，以晡時入見，易書而行。

translations.literal: He opened and looked—they were indeed different; he at once galloped back to the capital, entered audience in the late afternoon, had the letter changed, and set out.
translations.idiomatic: He opened it and found they did differ; he galloped straight back to the capital, was received in audience that afternoon, had the letter revised, and set out again.

sentences.zh: 及至，契丹不復求婚，專欲增幣，曰：「南朝遺我之辭當曰『獻』，否則曰『納』。」

translations.literal: When he arrived, the Khitan no longer sought marriage but wanted only increased tribute, saying: "The Southern Court's wording for what it gives us should read 'presented'—otherwise 'tendered.'"
translations.idiomatic: On his arrival the Khitan no longer asked for a marriage but pressed only for higher tribute, saying, "The Southern Court's wording for what it gives us must read xian ('presented')—otherwise na ('tendered')."

sentences.zh: 弼爭之，契丹主曰：「南朝既懼我矣，於二字何有？

translations.literal: Bi contested it; the Khitan ruler said: "The Southern Court already fears us—what matter are two characters?
translations.idiomatic: Bi resisted; the Khitan emperor said, "The Southern Court already fears us—what are two characters to you?

sentences.zh: 若我擁兵而南，得無悔乎！」

translations.literal: If I mass troops and march south, will you not regret it!"
translations.idiomatic: If I march south at the head of an army, will you not regret this!"

sentences.zh: 弼曰：「本朝兼愛南北，故不憚更成，何名為懼？

translations.literal: Bi said: "Our court cherishes both north and south alike, and therefore does not shrink from renewing the covenant—how is that called fear?
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "Our court cares equally for north and south, and therefore does not shrink from renewing the treaty—how is that fear?

sentences.zh: 或不得已至於用兵，則當以曲直為勝負，非使臣之所知也。」

translations.literal: If we are driven to arms, victory and defeat will be decided by right and wrong—that is not suited for an envoy to know."
translations.idiomatic: If matters come to war, right and wrong will decide the outcome—that is not suited for an envoy to say."

sentences.zh: 契丹主曰：「卿勿固執，古亦有之。」

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler said: "Do not be obstinate—there are precedents in antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Do not be stubborn—even antiquity offers precedents."

sentences.zh: 弼曰：「自古唯唐高祖借兵於突厥，當時贈遺，或稱獻納。

translations.literal: Bi said: "From antiquity only Tang Gaozu borrowed troops from the Turks; at that time gifts were sometimes called presented or tendered.
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "In all history only Gaozu of Tang borrowed troops from the Turks, and only then were gifts sometimes called presented or tendered.

sentences.zh: 其後頡利為太宗所擒，豈復有此禮哉！」

translations.literal: Afterward Jieli was captured by Taizong—how could such courtesy be used again!"
translations.idiomatic: After Jieli Khan was captured by Taizong, was such language ever used again?"

sentences.zh: 弼聲色俱厲，契丹知不可奪，乃曰：「吾當自遣人議之。」

translations.literal: Bi's voice and expression were both stern; the Khitan knew he could not be moved and said: "I shall send someone myself to negotiate."
translations.idiomatic: Bi's voice and bearing were fierce; seeing they could not shake him, the Khitan said, "I shall send envoys of my own to settle this."

sentences.zh: 復使劉六符來。

translations.literal: They again sent Liu Liufu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liufu was again sent south.

sentences.zh: 弼歸奏曰：「臣以死拒之，彼氣折矣，可勿許也。」

translations.literal: Bi returned and reported: "Your servant resisted to the death; their spirit was broken—they need not be granted this."
translations.idiomatic: On his return Bi reported, "I resisted even at the cost of my life; their spirit is broken—they need not be granted this point."

sentences.zh: 朝廷竟以「納」字與之。

translations.literal: The court in the end gave them the character "tendered."
translations.idiomatic: The court in the end conceded the word na ('tendered').

sentences.zh: 始受命，聞一女卒；

translations.literal: When he first received the commission he heard a daughter had died;
translations.idiomatic: When he first received his commission he learned that a daughter had died;

sentences.zh: 再命，聞一子生，皆不顧。

translations.literal: when he received the second commission he heard a son had been born—he paid no heed to either.
translations.idiomatic: when he was commissioned a second time he heard a son had been born—he gave neither event a thought.

sentences.zh: 又除樞密直學士，遷翰林學士，皆懇辭，曰：「增歲幣非臣本志，特以方討元昊，未暇與角，故不敢以死爭，其敢受乎！」

translations.literal: He was again appointed Academician Expositor-in-ordinary of the Bureau of Military Affairs and transferred to Hanlin Academician—all of which he earnestly declined, saying: "Increasing the annual tribute was not my original intent; only because we were then campaigning against Yuanhao and I had no leisure to contend to the death did I not dare die resisting—how then could I accept reward!"
translations.idiomatic: He was again made expositor-academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and promoted to Hanlin academician, but declined each post earnestly, saying, "Raising the annual tribute was never my intent; I did not fight to the death only because we were busy campaigning against Yuanhao—how then could I accept reward?"

sentences.zh: 三年，拜樞密副使，辭之愈力，改授資政殿學士兼侍讀學士。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; he declined with still greater force and was instead made Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Governance and concurrent Academician Reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qingli he was named vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; he declined with still greater force and was instead made academician of the Hall for Cultivating Governance and concurrent reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 七月，復拜樞密副使。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was again appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was again appointed vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 弼言：「契丹既結好，議者便謂無事，萬一敗盟，臣死且有罪。

translations.literal: Bi said: "Now that the Khitan have made peace, deliberators at once say there is nothing to do—yet if the alliance should fail, your servant would be guilty even in death.
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "Now that peace with the Khitan is settled, courtiers treat the frontier as settled—but if the treaty should fail, I would be guilty even in death.

sentences.zh: 願陛下思其輕侮之恥，坐薪嘗膽，不忘修政。」

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to recall the shame of their slight and insult, to sleep on brushwood and taste gall, and never forget to improve governance."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to remember the humiliation of their contempt, to sleep on brushwood and taste gall, and never cease to strengthen the realm."

sentences.zh: 以誥納上前而罷。

translations.literal: He presented the patent of appointment before the throne and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He laid the appointment patent before the throne and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 逾月，復申前命，使宰相諭之曰：「此朝廷特用，非以使遼故也。」

translations.literal: After more than a month the previous appointment was renewed; the chief councillors were sent to instruct him: "This is a special appointment by the court, not because of your mission to Liao."
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month the appointment was offered again, and the chief ministers were sent to tell him, "This is a special appointment by the court, not because of your embassy to Liao."

sentences.zh: 弼乃受。

translations.literal: Bi then accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Bi accept.

sentences.zh: 帝銳以太平責成宰輔，數下詔督弼與范仲淹等，又開天章閣，給筆札，使書其所欲為者；

translations.literal: The emperor keenly charged the chief ministers with bringing about peace and repeatedly issued edicts to urge Bi, Fan Zhongyan, and the others; he also opened the Tianzhang Pavilion, supplied brush and paper, and had them write what they wished to undertake;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor urgently looked to his chief ministers to deliver peace and repeatedly issued edicts pressing Bi, Fan Zhongyan, and the rest; he opened the Tianzhang Pavilion, supplied writing materials, and asked them to set down what they wished to accomplish;

sentences.zh: 且命仲淹主西事，弼主北事。

translations.literal: and moreover ordered Zhongyan to take charge of western affairs and Bi northern affairs.
translations.idiomatic: and ordered Zhongyan to take charge of western affairs and Bi of northern affairs.

sentences.zh: 弼上當世之務十餘條及安邊十三策，大略以進賢退不肖、止僥倖、去宿弊為本，欲漸易監司之不才者，使澄汰所部吏，於是小人始不悅矣。

translations.literal: Bi submitted more than ten items on the tasks of the age and thirteen strategies for securing the border, in general taking advancing the worthy and removing the unfit, stopping favoritism, and removing long-standing abuses as the foundation; he wished gradually to replace incompetent supervisory officials and have them clarify and weed out the clerks under them—thereupon petty men first became displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Bi submitted more than ten memoranda on the urgent business of the day and thirteen strategies for securing the borders, grounded chiefly in promoting the capable, removing the unfit, ending favoritism, and rooting out long-standing abuses; he sought gradually to replace incompetent regional supervisors and have them purge the clerks under their command—and from that point petty men first turned against him.

sentences.zh: 元昊遣使以書來，稱男不稱臣。

translations.literal: Yuanhao sent envoys with a letter that styled him "son" but not "subject."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhao sent envoys with a letter that addressed him as the emperor's son but not as his subject.

sentences.zh: 弼言：「契丹臣元昊而我不臣，則契丹為無敵於天下，不可許。」

translations.literal: Bi said: "If the Khitan treat Yuanhao as subject while we do not, then the Khitan will be without rival under Heaven—this cannot be permitted."
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "If the Khitan acknowledge Yuanhao as their subject while we do not, the Khitan will stand unrivaled under Heaven—that cannot be allowed."

sentences.zh: 乃卻其使，卒臣之。

translations.literal: He thereupon sent their envoys back, and in the end made Yuanhao submit.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the envoys back and in the end compelled Yuanhao to acknowledge Song suzerainty.

sentences.zh: 四年，契丹受禮雲中，且發兵會元昊伐呆兒族，於河東為近，帝疑二邊同謀。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Khitan received rites at Yunzhong and also sent troops to join Yuanhao in attacking the Daier tribe; as this was near Hedong, the emperor suspected collusion on both frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the Khitan held rites at Yunzhong and also sent troops to join Yuanhao against the Daier tribe; because this lay close to Hedong, the emperor suspected a joint plot on both frontiers.

sentences.zh: 弼曰：「兵出無名，契丹不為也。

translations.literal: Bi said: "To take the field without just cause—the Khitan would not do that.
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "The Khitan would not march without just cause.

sentences.zh: 元昊本與契丹約相左右，今契丹獨獲重幣，元昊有怨言，故城威塞以備之。

translations.literal: Yuanhao had originally agreed with the Khitan to support each other; now the Khitan alone received heavy tribute and Yuanhao had grievances, and therefore fortified Weisai to guard against them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhao had once pledged mutual support with the Khitan, but now the Khitan alone received heavy tribute while Yuanhao nursed grievances, and so he fortified Weisai against them.

sentences.zh: 呆兒屢寇威塞，契丹疑元昊使之，故為是役，安能合而寇我哉？」

translations.literal: The Daier repeatedly raided Weisai; the Khitan suspected Yuanhao had sent them, and therefore undertook this campaign—how could they unite to invade us?"
translations.idiomatic: The Daier had repeatedly raided Weisai, and the Khitan suspected Yuanhao of instigating them—this campaign was aimed at him, not at us. How could the two join to attack us?"

sentences.zh: 或請調發為備，弼曰：「如此正墮其計，臣請任之。」

translations.literal: Some urged mobilization as precaution; Bi said: "That would fall straight into their scheme—I ask to take responsibility."
translations.idiomatic: Some urged mobilizing troops in precaution; Bi said, "That would play straight into their scheme—let me take responsibility for this."

sentences.zh: 帝乃止，契丹卒不動。

translations.literal: The emperor then stopped, and the Khitan in the end did not move.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held back, and the Khitan in the end made no move.

sentences.zh: 夏竦不得志，中弼以飛語。

translations.literal: Xia Song, unable to achieve his aims, slandered Bi with whispered charges.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Song, frustrated in his ambitions, attacked Bi with whispered slanders.

sentences.zh: 弼懼，求宣撫河北，還，以資政殿學士出知鄆州。

translations.literal: Bi was afraid and requested appointment as pacification commissioner of Hebei; on his return he was made Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Governance and sent out as prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bi, alarmed, asked to be made pacification commissioner of Hebei; on his return he was made academician of the Hall for Cultivating Governance and sent out as prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，讒不驗，加給事中，移青州，兼京東路安撫使。

translations.literal: After more than a year the slanders were not borne out; he was given the additional title Supervising Censor and transferred to Qingzhou, concurrently serving as pacification commissioner of the Jingdong circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year the slanders proved false; he was given the additional title supervising censor, transferred to Qingzhou, and made concurrent pacification commissioner of the Jingdong circuit.

sentences.zh: 河朔大水，民流就食。

translations.literal: Great floods struck Heshuo and the people drifted about seeking food.
translations.idiomatic: Great floods struck the north of the Yellow River and the people wandered in search of food.

sentences.zh: 弼勸所部民出粟，益以官廩，得公私廬舍十餘萬區，散處其人，以便薪水。

translations.literal: Bi urged the people under his jurisdiction to contribute grain, supplemented it with government granaries, obtained more than one hundred thousand public and private lodgings, and scattered the refugees among them for convenience of fuel and water.
translations.idiomatic: Bi urged the people under his jurisdiction to contribute grain, supplemented it from government stores, secured more than one hundred thousand public and private buildings, and scattered the refugees among them so fuel and water would be easier to obtain.

sentences.zh: 官吏自前資、待缺、寄居者，皆賦以祿，使即民所聚，選老弱病瘠者廩之，仍書其勞，約他日為奏請受賞。

translations.literal: Officials whether of prior rank, awaiting appointment, or sojourning—all were given salaries and sent to where the people gathered; the old, weak, sick, and emaciated were selected for grain relief, their labor still recorded with a promise to memorialize later for reward.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of every status—former appointees, men awaiting posts, sojourners—were all paid salaries and sent to refugee camps; the old, weak, sick, and wasted were selected for grain relief, their service recorded with a promise of future reward.

sentences.zh: 率五日，輒遣人持酒肉飯糗慰藉，出於至誠，人人為儘力。

translations.literal: Every five days on average he sent men bearing wine, meat, rice, and dry provisions to comfort them; proceeding from utmost sincerity, everyone exerted himself to the full.
translations.idiomatic: Every five days or so he sent men with wine, meat, rice, and dry provisions to comfort them; his sincerity was so complete that everyone gave his utmost.

sentences.zh: 山林陂澤之利可資以生者，聽流民擅取。

translations.literal: The benefits of hills, forests, marshes, and lakes that could sustain life were permitted to be taken freely by the refugees.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees were allowed to take freely whatever the hills, forests, marshes, and lakes could provide for their livelihood.

sentences.zh: 死者為大冢葬之，目曰「叢冢」。

translations.literal: The dead were buried in great mounds called "the clustered tombs."
translations.idiomatic: The dead were buried in great mounds called the Clustered Tombs.

sentences.zh: 明年，麥大熟，民各以遠近受糧歸，凡活五十餘萬人，募為兵者萬計。

translations.literal: The next year wheat ripened abundantly; the people each according to distance received grain and returned home—in all more than five hundred thousand lives were saved, and those recruited as soldiers numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the wheat crop was abundant; people returned home according to distance to receive grain—in all more than five hundred thousand lives were saved, and those recruited as soldiers numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，遣使褒勞，拜禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he sent envoys to praise and comfort him and appointed him Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this he sent envoys to praise and comfort him and appointed him vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 弼曰：「此守臣職也。」

translations.literal: Bi said: "This is a defending official's duty."
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "That is simply a local official's duty."

sentences.zh: 辭不受。

translations.literal: He declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He declined and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 前此，救災者皆聚民城郭中，為粥食之，蒸為疾疫，及相蹈藉，或待哺數日不得粥而仆，名為救之，而實殺之。

translations.literal: Before this, those who relieved disasters all gathered the people inside walled towns and fed them porridge; steam bred pestilence and they trampled one another, or waited days for porridge without receiving it and collapsed—called saving them, but in fact killing them.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, relief efforts had always herded refugees inside walled towns and fed them porridge; pestilence spread, people trampled one another, and some waited days without a bowl and collapsed—in name they were saved, in fact they were killed.

sentences.zh: 自弼立法簡便周盡，天下傳以為式。

translations.literal: From Bi's laws, simple, convenient, and thorough, the empire took them as a model.
translations.idiomatic: Bi's methods—simple, thorough, and complete—were taken as the model throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 王則叛，齊州禁兵欲應之，或詣弼告。

translations.literal: When Wang Ze rebelled, the garrison troops of Qizhou wished to join him; someone came to inform Bi.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Ze rebelled, the garrison troops of Qizhou were ready to join him, and someone came to warn Bi.

sentences.zh: 齊非弼所部，恐事泄變生，適中貴人張從訓銜命至青，弼度其可用，密付以事，使馳至齊，發吏卒取之，無得脫者。

translations.literal: Qi was not under Bi's jurisdiction; fearing the matter would leak and change arise, it happened that the palace favorite Zhang Congxun arrived at Qing on imperial commission; Bi judged him usable, secretly entrusted him with the affair, and had him gallop to Qi, where he mobilized clerks and soldiers to seize them—not one escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Qizhou was outside Bi's jurisdiction, and he feared that if word leaked the situation would turn violent; just then the palace favorite Zhang Congxun arrived at Qing on imperial business. Bi judged him reliable, secretly entrusted him with the matter, and had him gallop to Qizhou to seize the conspirators with local troops—not one escaped.

sentences.zh: 即自劾顓擅之罪，帝益嘉之，復以為禮部侍郎，又辭不受。

translations.literal: He at once impeached himself for the offense of acting on his own authority; the emperor praised him all the more, again appointed him Vice Minister of Rites, and again he declined.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately impeached himself for acting on his own authority; the emperor praised him all the more, again offered him the post of vice minister of rites, and again he declined.

sentences.zh: 遷大學士，徙知鄭、蔡、河陽，加觀文殿學士，改宣徽南院使、判幷州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Academician, moved to administer Zheng, Cai, and Heyang, given the additional title Academician of the Hall for Viewing Culture, and changed to Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Domestic Service with concurrent administration of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand academician, served in turn as prefect of Zheng, Cai, and Heyang, was made academician of the Hall for Viewing Culture, and was appointed commissioner of the southern bureau of the palace domestic service with concurrent administration of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 至和二年，召拜同中書門下平章事、集賢殿大學士，與文彥博並命。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhihe he was summoned and appointed Associate Chief Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery and Grand Academician of the Hall for Assembling the Worthy, appointed together with Wen Yanbo.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhihe 2 (1055) he was summoned and appointed associate chief councillor and grand academician of the Hall for Assembling the Worthy, on the same day as Wen Yanbo.

sentences.zh: 宣制之日，士大夫相慶於朝。

translations.literal: On the day the appointment was proclaimed, scholar-officials congratulated one another at court.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the appointments were proclaimed, the scholar-officials congratulated one another throughout the court.

sentences.zh: 帝微覘知之，以語學士歐陽修曰：「古之命相，或得諸夢卜，豈若今日人情如此哉？」

translations.literal: The emperor glimpsed this in secret and said to Academician Ouyang Xiu: "In antiquity appointing a chief councillor sometimes came from dreams or divination—how can it compare with popular feeling today such as this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor noticed this in secret and said to academician Ouyang Xiu, "In antiquity chief ministers were sometimes chosen by dreams or divination—how can that compare with the feeling at court today?"

sentences.zh: 修頓首賀。

translations.literal: Xiu kowtowed in congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu kowtowed in congratulation.

sentences.zh: 帝弗豫，大臣不得見，中外憂慄。

translations.literal: When the emperor fell ill, the great ministers could not see him; inside and outside the court were anxious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill the chief ministers could not see him, and anxiety spread through court and country.

sentences.zh: 弼、彥博入問疾，因託禳禬事止宿連夕，每事皆關白乃行，宮內肅然，語在《彥博傳》。

translations.literal: Bi and Yanbo entered to inquire after his illness and, on the pretext of exorcism and prayer, lodged overnight for successive evenings; every matter had to be reported before action—within the palace all was orderly, as told in the Biography of Yanbo.
translations.idiomatic: Bi and Yanbo went in to inquire after his health and, on the pretext of performing exorcisms, lodged in the palace night after night; every matter had to be reported before it was carried out, and order was restored within the palace—the account is in Yanbo's biography.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐三年，進昭文館大學士、監修國史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiayou he was advanced to Grand Academician of the Hall of Brilliance in Literature and Supervisor of the compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiayou 3 (1058) he was advanced to grand academician of the Hall of Brilliance in Literature and supervisor of the national history.

sentences.zh: 弼為相，守典故，行故事，而傅以公議，無容心於其間。

translations.literal: As chief councillor Bi observed precedents, followed established practice, and clothed it in public deliberation, without private inclination in between.
translations.idiomatic: As chief councillor Bi observed precedent, followed established practice, and grounded every decision in open deliberation, without private inclination.

sentences.zh: 當是時，百官任職，天下無事。

translations.literal: At that time the hundred officials fulfilled their duties and the realm was without incident.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the officials fulfilled their duties and the realm was at peace.

sentences.zh: 六年三月，以母憂去位，詔為罷春宴。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year he left office on account of mourning for his mother; an edict canceled the spring banquet on his account.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the sixth year he left office to mourn his mother, and an edict canceled the spring banquet on his account.

sentences.zh: 故事，執政遭喪皆起復。

translations.literal: By precedent, chief administrators who encountered bereavement were all recalled from mourning.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, chief administrators in mourning were always recalled to office.

sentences.zh: 帝虛位五起之，弼謂此金革變禮，不可施於平世，卒不從命。

translations.literal: The emperor left the post vacant and summoned him five times; Bi said this was the altered rite of arms and could not be applied in a peaceful age, and in the end did not obey.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor left the post vacant and summoned him five times; Bi held that this wartime exception to mourning could not be applied in a peaceful age, and in the end refused.

sentences.zh: 英宗立，召為樞密使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong ascended, Bi was summoned as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong ascended the throne, Bi was summoned as commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 居二年，以足疾求解，拜鎮海軍節度使、同中書門下平章事、判揚州，封祁國公，進封鄭。

translations.literal: After two years, on account of foot ailment he sought release, was appointed Military Commissioner of the Zhenhai army, Associate Chief Councillor, and concurrent administrator of Yangzhou, enfeoffed as Duke of Qi, and advanced to Duke of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he asked to retire on account of foot ailment, was appointed military commissioner of the Zhenhai army, associate chief councillor, and concurrent administrator of Yangzhou, enfeoffed as Duke of Qi, and later advanced to Duke of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 熙寧元年，徙判汝州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xining he was transferred to concurrent administration of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 1 (1068) he was transferred to concurrent administration of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔入覲，許肩輿至殿門。

translations.literal: He was ordered to attend audience and permitted a sedan chair as far as the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to attend audience and permitted a sedan chair as far as the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 神宗御內東門小殿，令其子掖以進，且命毋拜，坐語，從容訪以治道。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong received him in the small hall at the inner eastern gate, had his son support him in entering, and moreover ordered that he not bow; they sat and conversed, and the emperor unhurriedly inquired about the way of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong received him in the small hall at the inner eastern gate, had his son support him as he entered, ordered that he not bow, and sat with him in conversation, calmly inquiring about the way of governance.

sentences.zh: 弼知帝果於有為，對曰：「人主好惡，不可令人窺測；

translations.literal: Bi knew the emperor was resolute in action and replied: "A ruler's likes and dislikes must not be allowed to be fathomed by others;
translations.idiomatic: Bi knew the emperor was determined to act and replied, "A ruler's likes and dislikes must not be legible to others;

sentences.zh: 可測，則奸人得以傅會。

translations.literal: if they can be measured, then wicked men can attach themselves by coincidence.
translations.idiomatic: if they can be read, wicked men will attach themselves to them.

sentences.zh: 當如天之監人，善惡皆所自取，然後誅賞隨之，則功罪無不得其實矣。」

translations.literal: He should be like Heaven overseeing men—good and evil are all taken by themselves—then punishments and rewards follow, and merit and fault will none fail to receive their true measure."
translations.idiomatic: He should be like Heaven watching over men, from whom good and evil are freely chosen; only then should punishments and rewards follow, so that merit and fault receive their true measure."

sentences.zh: 又問邊事，對曰：「陛下臨御未久，當布德行惠，願二十年口不言兵。」

translations.literal: Asked again about frontier affairs, he replied: "Your Majesty has not long held the throne; you should spread virtue and bestow kindness—I wish that for twenty years you would not speak of arms."
translations.idiomatic: Asked about frontier affairs, he replied, "Your Majesty has not long held the throne; you should spread virtue and bestow kindness—I beg that for twenty years you will not speak of war."

sentences.zh: 帝默然。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was silent.

sentences.zh: 至日昃乃退。

translations.literal: Only when the sun slanted did he withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew only when the sun was setting.

sentences.zh: 欲以集禧觀使留之，力辭赴郡。

translations.literal: They wished to keep him as Commissioner of the Jixi Abbey, but he forcefully declined and went to his prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The court wished to keep him as commissioner of the Jixi Abbey, but he firmly declined and went to his post.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，召拜司空兼侍中，賜甲第，悉辭之，以左僕射、門下侍郎同平章事。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year he was summoned and appointed Minister of Works with concurrent Palace Attendant, granted a fine mansion—all of which he declined—and made Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Vice Director of the Chancellery, and Associate Chief Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year he was summoned as minister of works and palace attendant and offered a fine mansion—all of which he declined—and was made left vice director of the Imperial Secretariat, vice director of the Chancellery, and associate chief councillor.

sentences.zh: 時有為帝言災異皆天數，非關人事得失所致者。

translations.literal: At the time someone told the emperor that portents and anomalies were all Heaven's numbers and had nothing to do with human affairs' gain or loss.
translations.idiomatic: At the time someone told the emperor that omens and anomalies were all Heaven's fixed decree and had nothing to do with human conduct.

sentences.zh: 弼聞而歎曰：「人君所畏惟天，若不畏天，何事不可為者！

translations.literal: When Bi heard it he sighed and said: "What a ruler fears is only Heaven—if he does not fear Heaven, what may he not do!
translations.idiomatic: When Bi heard this he sighed and said, "What a ruler should fear is Heaven alone—if he does not fear Heaven, what act will be beyond him?

sentences.zh: 此必奸人欲進邪說，以搖上心，使輔拂諫爭之臣，無所施其力。

translations.literal: This must be wicked men wishing to advance perverse doctrines to shake the sovereign's mind and render assisting, admonishing, and disputing ministers unable to exert their strength.
translations.idiomatic: This must be wicked men seeking to advance perverse doctrines, shake the sovereign's mind, and render loyal remonstrators powerless.

sentences.zh: 是治亂之機，不可以不速救。」

translations.literal: This is the hinge of order and chaos and must be swiftly remedied."
translations.idiomatic: This strikes at the hinge of order and chaos and must be remedied at once."

sentences.zh: 即上書數千言，力論之。

translations.literal: He at once submitted a memorial of several thousand characters arguing the point forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: He at once submitted a memorial of several thousand characters arguing the point at length.

sentences.zh: 又言：「君子小人之進退，繫王道之消長，願深加辨察，勿以同異為喜怒、喜怒為用舍。

translations.literal: He also said: "The advancement and withdrawal of gentlemen and petty men is tied to the waxing and waning of the kingly way—I beg deep discrimination, and that you not make likes and dislikes out of agreement and disagreement, nor appointment and dismissal out of likes and dislikes.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Whether gentlemen or petty men rise or fall bears on the waxing and waning of the kingly way—I beg Your Majesty to judge deeply and not to make likes and dislikes out of agreement and disagreement, nor appointments out of likes and dislikes.

sentences.zh: 陛下好使人伺察外事，故奸險得志。

translations.literal: Your Majesty likes to have men spy on outside affairs, and therefore the treacherous achieve their aims.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty likes to have men spy on affairs outside the court, and therefore the treacherous prosper.

sentences.zh: 又多出親批，若事事皆中，亦非為君之道；

translations.literal: You also issue many personal rescripts; even if every matter hits the mark, that is still not the way of ruling;
translations.idiomatic: You also issue many personal rescripts; even if every decision were correct, that would still not be the way to rule;

sentences.zh: 脫十中七八，積日累月，所失亦多。

translations.literal: if only seven or eight of ten hit the mark, over days and months the losses are also many.
translations.idiomatic: and if only seven or eight of ten are right, the losses over days and months will still be great.

sentences.zh: 今中外之務漸有更張，大抵小人惟喜生事，願深燭其然，無使有悔。」

translations.literal: Now affairs inside and outside are gradually being changed; in general petty men only delight in stirring trouble—I beg you to illuminate this deeply and not allow regret."
translations.idiomatic: Affairs at court and in the provinces are now being changed; petty men generally delight only in stirring trouble—I beg Your Majesty to see this clearly and not allow regret."

sentences.zh: 是時久旱，群臣請上尊號及用樂，帝不許，而以同天節契丹使當上壽，故未斷其請。

translations.literal: At that time drought had long continued; the ministers requested an honorific title and the use of music—the emperor did not permit it, but because Khitan envoys for the Tongtian festival were due to offer birthday felicitations, he had not yet decided their request.
translations.idiomatic: Drought had long continued; the ministers asked that an honorific title be adopted and music be used—the emperor refused, but because Khitan envoys for the Tongtian festival were due to offer birthday felicitations, he had not yet ruled on their request.

sentences.zh: 弼言此盛德事，正當以此示之，乞並罷上壽。

translations.literal: Bi said this was a matter of great virtue and should be shown by this very act—he begged that birthday felicitations also be canceled.
translations.idiomatic: Bi said this was precisely the moment to display great virtue and begged that the birthday felicitations also be canceled.

sentences.zh: 帝從之，即日雨。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his advice, and that very day it rained.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and rain fell that very day.

sentences.zh: 弼又上疏，願益畏天戒，遠奸佞，近忠良。

translations.literal: Bi again submitted a memorial, wishing that the emperor would further fear Heaven's warnings, keep distant from the treacherous and fawning, and draw near the loyal and good.
translations.idiomatic: Bi submitted another memorial urging the emperor to fear Heaven's warnings all the more, keep the treacherous at a distance, and draw the loyal near.

sentences.zh: 帝手詔褒答之。

translations.literal: The emperor personally drafted an edict in praise to reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied with a personal edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 王安石用事，雅不與弼合。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi held power and had never been in accord with Bi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi held power and had never been in accord with Bi.

sentences.zh: 弼度不能爭，多稱疾求退，章數十上。

translations.literal: Bi judged that he could not contend and often pleaded illness to seek withdrawal, submitting memorials several tens of times.
translations.idiomatic: Bi judged that he could not prevail and repeatedly pleaded illness to retire, submitting dozens of memorials.

sentences.zh: 神宗將許之，問曰：「卿即去，誰可代卿者？」

translations.literal: Shenzong was about to grant it and asked: "If you leave, who can replace you?"
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong was about to grant his request and asked, "If you go, who can replace you?"

sentences.zh: 弼薦文彥博，神宗默然，良久曰：「王安石何如？」

translations.literal: Bi recommended Wen Yanbo; Shenzong was silent, and after a long while said: "What of Wang Anshi?"
translations.idiomatic: Bi recommended Wen Yanbo. Shenzong was silent, and after a long pause said, "What of Wang Anshi?"

sentences.zh: 弼亦默然。

translations.literal: Bi too was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Bi too was silent.

sentences.zh: 拜武寧節度使、同中書門下平章事、判河南，改亳州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Military Commissioner of the Wuning army, Associate Chief Councillor, and concurrent administrator of Henan, then transferred to Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military commissioner of the Wuning army, associate chief councillor, and concurrent administrator of Henan, then transferred to Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 青苗法出，弼以謂如是則財聚於上，人散於下，持不行。

translations.literal: When the Green Sprouts law was promulgated, Bi held that if so wealth would gather above and people scatter below, and he refused to implement it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Green Sprouts law was promulgated, Bi held that it would concentrate wealth at the top and scatter the people below, and he refused to implement it.

sentences.zh: 提舉官趙濟劾弼格詔旨，侍御史鄧綰又乞付有司鞫治，乃以僕射判汝州。

translations.literal: The intendant Zhao Ji impeached Bi for resisting the imperial edict; the Attending Censor Deng Guan again asked that he be handed to the authorities for investigation—thereupon he was made Vice Director with concurrent administration of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Intendant Zhao Ji impeached Bi for defying the edict; attending censor Deng Guan asked that he be handed over for investigation—whereupon he was made vice director with concurrent administration of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 安石曰：「弼雖責，猶不失富貴。

translations.literal: Anshi said: "Though Bi is punished, he still does not lose wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi said, "Though Bi is punished, he still keeps his wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 昔鯀以方命殛，共工以象恭流，弼兼此二罪，止奪使相，何由沮奸？」

translations.literal: Formerly Gun was executed for defying orders and Gong Gong was banished for specious respect—Bi combines both offenses, yet is only stripped of envoy and chief councillor—how can treachery be deterred?"
translations.idiomatic: Gun was executed for defying orders and Gong Gong was banished for hollow courtesy—Bi has committed both offenses, yet loses only his envoy and chief councillor posts—how will treachery be deterred?"

sentences.zh: 帝不答。

translations.literal: The emperor did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not reply.

sentences.zh: 弼言：「新法，臣所不曉，不可以治郡。

translations.literal: Bi said: "The new laws are what your servant does not understand—I cannot use them to govern a prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "The new laws are what I do not understand—I cannot govern a prefecture by them.

sentences.zh: 願歸洛養疾。」

translations.literal: I wish to return to Luoyang and nurse my illness."
translations.idiomatic: I wish to return to Luoyang and nurse my illness."

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: This was granted.
translations.idiomatic: This was granted.

sentences.zh: 遂請老，加拜司空，進封韓國公致仕。

translations.literal: He then requested retirement on account of age, was further appointed Minister of Works, advanced to Duke of Han, and retired.
translations.idiomatic: He then requested retirement on account of age, was further appointed minister of works, advanced to Duke of Han, and retired from office.

sentences.zh: 弼雖家居，朝廷有大利害，知無不言。

translations.literal: Though Bi lived at home, whenever the court had great benefit or harm he knew of it and spoke without reserve.
translations.idiomatic: Though he lived in retirement, whenever the court faced grave matters he spoke without reserve.

sentences.zh: 郭逵討安南，乞詔逵擇利進退，以全王師；

translations.literal: When Guo Kui campaigned against Annan, he begged that an edict order Kui to advance or withdraw according to advantage to preserve the imperial army;
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Kui campaigned against Annan, he asked that the emperor order Kui to advance or withdraw as advantage dictated, so as to preserve the imperial army;

sentences.zh: 契丹爭河東地界，言其不可許；

translations.literal: when the Khitan disputed the Hedong boundary, he said it could not be granted;
translations.idiomatic: when the Khitan disputed the Hedong boundary, he said it must not be conceded;

sentences.zh: 星文有變，乞開廣言路；

translations.literal: when astral signs changed, he begged to open and broaden the path of speech;
translations.idiomatic: when the stars showed anomalies, he asked that the path of remonstrance be widened;

sentences.zh: 又請速改新法，以解倒縣之急。

translations.literal: and again asked that the new laws be swiftly changed to relieve the urgency of the inverted state.
translations.idiomatic: and again urged that the new laws be changed at once to relieve the empire's desperate strain.

sentences.zh: 帝雖不盡用，而眷禮不衰，嘗因安石有所建明，卻之曰：「富弼手疏稱『老臣無所告訴，但仰屋竊歎』者，即當至矣。」

translations.literal: Though the emperor did not employ all his advice, favor and courtesy did not decline; once when Anshi made some proposal, he rejected it saying: "The hand memorial from Fu Bi saying 'the old minister has nowhere to appeal, but only looks up at the roof and sighs in secret'—that will soon arrive."
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor did not follow all his advice, his favor never waned; once when Anshi made some proposal, the emperor rejected it, saying, "Fu Bi's private memorial saying 'this old minister has nowhere to turn but looks up at the rafters and sighs' will soon arrive."

sentences.zh: 其敬之如此。

translations.literal: Such was the respect shown him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the respect in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 元豐三年，王堯臣之子同老上言：「故父參知政事時，當仁宗服藥，嘗與弼及文彥博議立儲嗣，會翌日有瘳，其事遂寢。」

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanfeng, Wang Yaochen's son Tonglao submitted a statement: "When my late father was Associate Chief Councillor, as Emperor Renzong took medicine, he once with Bi and Wen Yanbo deliberated establishing an heir; it happened that the next day there was recovery, and the matter was then laid aside."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanfeng (1080), Wang Yaochen's son Tonglao submitted a statement: "When my late father was associate chief councillor, during Emperor Renzong's illness he once deliberated with Bi and Wen Yanbo on establishing an heir; the emperor recovered the next day and the matter was dropped."

sentences.zh: 帝以問彥博，對與同老合，帝始知至和時事。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned Yanbo; his reply agreed with Tonglao, and the emperor first learned of the affairs of the Zhihe period.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned Yanbo; his account agreed with Tonglao's, and the emperor first learned what had happened in the Zhihe period.

sentences.zh: 嘉弼不自言，以為司徒。

translations.literal: He praised Bi for not speaking of it himself and appointed him Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He praised Bi for never having spoken of it himself and appointed him minister of education.

sentences.zh: 六年八月，薨，年八十。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the sixth year he died, aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the sixth year he died, aged eighty.

sentences.zh: 手封遺奏，使其子紹庭上之。

translations.literal: He personally sealed a final memorial and had his son Shaoting present it.
translations.idiomatic: He personally sealed a final memorial and had his son Shaoting present it.

sentences.zh: 其大略云：

translations.literal: Its general purport said:
translations.idiomatic: Its general purport was as follows:

sentences.zh: 「陛下即位之初，邪臣納說圖任之際，聽受失宜，上誤聰明，浸成禍患。

translations.literal: "At the beginning of Your Majesty's accession, when wicked ministers offered doctrines and plotted appointments, what was heard and accepted was improper, above misleading clear wisdom, and gradually forming calamity.
translations.idiomatic: "At the beginning of Your Majesty's reign, when wicked ministers offered doctrines and plotted for office, what was heard and accepted was wrong, Your Majesty's judgment was misled, and calamity gradually took shape.

sentences.zh: 今上自輔臣，下及多士，畏禍圖利，習成敝風，忠詞讜論，無復上達。

translations.literal: Now from chief ministers above down to the many scholars, all fear disaster and scheme for profit; a corrupt custom has formed, and loyal words and forthright discourse no longer reach above.
translations.idiomatic: Now from the chief ministers down to the scholar-officials, all fear disaster and scheme for profit; a corrupt custom has taken hold, and loyal remonstrance no longer reaches the throne.

sentences.zh: 臣老病將死，尚何顧求？

translations.literal: Your servant is old, ill, and about to die—what is there still to seek or care for?
translations.idiomatic: I am old, ill, and about to die—what is there left for me to seek?

sentences.zh: 特以不忍上負聖明，輒傾肝膽，冀哀憐愚忠，曲垂採納。

translations.literal: Only because I cannot bear to fail Your Sagely Brightness above do I pour out liver and gall, hoping you will pity foolish loyalty and bend to adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: Only because I cannot bear to fail Your Sagely Majesty do I pour out my heart, hoping you will pity this foolish loyalty and deign to accept it.

sentences.zh: 去年永樂之役，兵民死亡者數十萬。

translations.literal: In last year's Yongle campaign, soldiers and civilians who died numbered several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In last year's Yongle campaign, several hundred thousand soldiers and civilians died.

sentences.zh: 今久戍未解，百姓困窮，豈諱過恥敗，不思救禍之時乎？

translations.literal: Now long garrison without relief—the people are trapped in poverty—is this the time to conceal faults, be shamed by defeat, and not think of saving from calamity?
translations.idiomatic: Long campaigns drag on without end and the people are destitute—is this the time to hide mistakes, shrink from defeat, and refuse to think of saving the realm from disaster?

sentences.zh: 天地至仁，寧與羌夷校曲直勝負？

translations.literal: Heaven and earth are supremely benevolent—would they contend right and wrong and victory and defeat with Qiang and Yi?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth are supremely benevolent—would they settle right and wrong in contest with frontier tribes?

sentences.zh: 願歸其侵地，休兵息民，使關、陝之間，稍遂生理。

translations.literal: I wish to return their invaded lands, rest the troops and give the people peace, and let between the passes and Shaanxi livelihood gradually be restored.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that their seized lands be returned, the armies rested and the people given peace, so that between the passes and Shaanxi life may gradually return to normal.

sentences.zh: 兼陝西再團保甲，又葺教場，州縣奉行，勢侔星火，人情惶駭，難以復用，不若寢罷以綏懷之。

translations.literal: Moreover in Shaanxi the baojia militia are again mustered and drill grounds repaired; prefectures and counties carry this out with force like sparks flying—popular feeling is terrified and alarmed, hard to employ again—it would be better to let it sleep and cease so as to soothe and embrace them.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Shaanxi is again mustering baojia militia and repairing drill grounds; prefectures and counties carry this out with meteoric urgency, and the people are terrified—it cannot be sustained. Better to let these measures lapse and soothe the people instead.

sentences.zh: 臣之所陳，急於濟事。

translations.literal: What your servant has stated is urgent for accomplishing the task.
translations.idiomatic: What I have stated bears urgently on practical relief.

sentences.zh: 若夫要道，則在聖人所存，與所用之人君子、小人之辨耳。

translations.literal: As for the essential way, it lies in what the sage holds in mind and the distinction between gentlemen and petty men among those employed.
translations.idiomatic: The essential way, however, lies in what the sage holds in mind and in distinguishing gentlemen from petty men among those he employs.

sentences.zh: 陛下審觀天下之勢，豈以為無足慮邪？」

translations.literal: Your Majesty should carefully observe the trend of the realm—do you think it is not worth concern?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should carefully observe the trend of the realm—do you think it is not worth concern?"

sentences.zh: 帝覽奏震悼，輟朝三日，內出祭文致奠，贈太尉，諡曰文忠。

translations.literal: When the emperor read the memorial he was shaken and grieved, suspended court for three days, issued from within a funerary text to offer sacrifice, posthumously granted Grand Guardian, and gave the posthumous title Wenzong (Cultured and Loyal).
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor read the memorial he was shaken with grief, suspended court for three days, issued a funerary text from within the palace, posthumously granted him grand guardian, and gave him the posthumous title Cultured and Loyal.

sentences.zh: 弼性至孝，恭儉好修，與人言必盡敬，雖微官及布衣謁見，皆與之亢禮，氣色穆然，不見喜慍。

translations.literal: Bi by nature was supremely filial, respectful and frugal and fond of cultivation; in speaking with others he was always fully reverent—even when minor officials and commoners in plain dress came to call, he met them with equal courtesy; his bearing was grave and composed, with no sign of joy or anger.
translations.idiomatic: Bi was profoundly filial by nature, respectful, frugal, and devoted to self-cultivation; in conversation he was always fully courteous—even minor officials and commoners in plain dress received equal treatment; his bearing was grave and serene, with no sign of joy or anger.

sentences.zh: 其好善嫉惡，出於天資。

translations.literal: His love of good and hatred of evil sprang from inborn nature.
translations.idiomatic: His love of good and hatred of evil sprang from inborn nature.

sentences.zh: 常言：「君子與小人並處，其勢必不勝。

translations.literal: He often said: "When gentlemen and petty men dwell together, the gentleman by force of circumstance cannot prevail.
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "When gentlemen and petty men dwell together, the gentleman cannot prevail.

sentences.zh: 君子不勝，則奉身而退，樂道無悶。

translations.literal: If the gentleman does not prevail, he withdraws with his person intact and delights in the Way without vexation.
translations.idiomatic: If the gentleman does not prevail, he withdraws with dignity and delights in the Way without vexation.

sentences.zh: 小人不勝，則交結構扇，千岐萬轍，必勝而後已。

translations.literal: If the petty man does not prevail, he forms cliques and stirs factions by a thousand forks and ten thousand tracks, and will not stop until victorious.
translations.idiomatic: If the petty man does not prevail, he forms cliques and stirs factions by every means, and will not stop until he wins.

sentences.zh: 迨其得志，遂肆毒於善良，求天下不亂，不可得也。」

translations.literal: When they achieve their aims, they then unleash poison on the good—to seek that the realm not fall into chaos is impossible."
translations.idiomatic: When they achieve their aims, they unleash poison on the good—then to seek that the realm not fall into chaos is impossible."

sentences.zh: 其終身皆出於此云。

translations.literal: His whole life issued from this, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: His whole life issued from this principle.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，配享神宗廟庭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou he was granted joint sacrifice in Emperor Shenzong's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanyou he was granted joint sacrifice in Emperor Shenzong's temple.

sentences.zh: 哲宗篆其碑首曰：「顯忠尚德」，命學士蘇軾撰文刻之。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhezong inscribed the stele head "Manifest Loyalty and Esteem Virtue" and ordered Academician Su Shi to compose the text and carve it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhezong inscribed the stele head Manifest Loyalty and Esteem Virtue and ordered academician Su Shi to compose and carve the text.

sentences.zh: 紹聖中，章惇執政，謂弼得罪先帝，罷配享。

translations.literal: During Shaosheng, Zhang Dun held power and said Bi had offended the late emperor; joint sacrifice was revoked.
translations.idiomatic: During Shaosheng, Zhang Dun held power and said Bi had offended the late emperor; his joint sacrifice was revoked.

sentences.zh: 至靖康初，詔復舊典焉。

translations.literal: By the beginning of Jingkang an edict restored the former rite.
translations.idiomatic: By the beginning of Jingkang an edict restored the former rite.

sentences.zh: 子 紹庭

translations.literal: Son: Shaoting
translations.idiomatic: Son: Shaoting

sentences.zh: 紹庭，字德先，性靖重，能守家法。

translations.literal: Shaoting, styled Dexian, was by nature calm and weighty and able to uphold the family rules.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoting, whose style name was Dexian, was calm and weighty by nature and able to uphold the family rules.

sentences.zh: 弼薨，兩女與婿及甥皆同居，紹庭待之與父時不殊，一家之事毫髮不敢變，族里稱焉。

translations.literal: When Bi died, two daughters with sons-in-law and nephews all lived together; Shaoting treated them no differently than in his father's time, not daring to alter a hair of the household's affairs—the clan praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When Bi died, two daughters with their husbands and nephews all lived together; Shaoting treated them exactly as in his father's day and did not dare alter the slightest household custom—the clan praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 歷宗正丞、提舉三門白波輦運、通判絳州。

translations.literal: He served as Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court, intendant of the Sanmen Baibo imperial transport, and vice prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice director of the imperial clan court, intendant of the Sanmen Baibo imperial transport, and vice prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 建中靖國初，除提舉河北西路常平，辭曰：「熙寧變法之初，先臣以不行青苗被罪，臣不敢為此官。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong Jingguo he was appointed intendant of the Hebei West circuit Ever-Normal Granaries but declined, saying: "At the beginning of the Xining reforms my late father was punished for not implementing Green Sprouts—I dare not hold this office."
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianzhong Jingguo he was appointed intendant of the Hebei West circuit Ever-Normal Granaries but declined, saying, "At the beginning of the Xining reforms my late father was punished for refusing to implement the Green Sprouts law—I dare not hold this office."

sentences.zh: 徽宗嘉之，擢祠部員外郎。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong praised this and promoted him to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong praised this and promoted him to vice director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出知宿州。

translations.literal: Before long he went out as prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was sent out as prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died, aged sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 子直柔，紹興中，同知樞密院事，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Zhirou, in the Shaoxing period Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhirou, who in the Shaoxing period served as vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 文彥博

translations.literal: Wen Yanbo
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yanbo

sentences.zh: 文彥博，字寬夫，汾州介休人。

translations.literal: Wen Yanbo, styled Kuanfu, was a man of Jiexiu in Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yanbo, whose style name was Kuanfu, came from Jiexiu in Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 其先本敬氏，以避晉高祖及宋翼祖諱改焉。

translations.literal: His ancestors were originally of the Jing clan and changed the name to avoid the taboo names of Jin Gaozu and the Song dynasty's Founder Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors were originally of the Jing clan and changed the name to avoid the taboo names of Jin Gaozu and the Song founder ancestor.

sentences.zh: 少與張昪、高若訥從潁昌史炤學，炤母異之，曰：「貴人也。」

translations.literal: In youth he with Zhang Bian and Gao Ruonuo studied under Shi Zhao of Yingchang; Zhao's mother marveled at him and said: "A noble man."
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied with Zhang Bian and Gao Ruonuo under Shi Zhao of Yingchang; Zhao's mother marveled at him and said, "Here is a man of rank."

sentences.zh: 待之甚厚。

translations.literal: She treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: She treated him with great generosity.

sentences.zh: 及進士第，知翼城縣，通判絳州，為監察御史，轉殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: After attaining the jinshi degree he was magistrate of Yicheng county, vice prefect of Jiangzhou, made Investigating Censor, and transferred to Attending Censor within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After attaining the jinshi degree he was magistrate of Yicheng county, vice prefect of Jiangzhou, made investigating censor, and transferred to attending censor within the palace.

sentences.zh: 西方用兵，偏校有監陳先退、望敵不進者，大將守著令皆申覆。

translations.literal: When arms were used in the west, among deputy commanders some supervised the array and retreated first or gazed at the enemy without advancing; the great generals adhered to orders and all submitted reports for review.
translations.idiomatic: When war was waged in the west, some deputy commanders supervised the line but retreated first or faced the enemy without advancing; the senior generals followed regulations and submitted every case for higher review.

sentences.zh: 彥博言：「此可施之平居無事時爾。

translations.literal: Yanbo said: "This may be applied in peaceful times when nothing is amiss.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo said, "That may do in peaceful times when nothing is amiss.
