sentences.zh: 今擁兵數十萬，而將權不專，兵法不峻，將何以濟？」

translations.literal: Now with several hundred thousand troops in hand, yet command authority is not exclusive and military law is not stern—how will it succeed?"
translations.idiomatic: Now we field several hundred thousand troops, yet command is not unified and military law is not strict—how can that succeed?"

sentences.zh: 仁宗嘉納之。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong praised and adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong praised and adopted his advice.

sentences.zh: 黃德和之誣劉平降虜也，以金帶賂平奴，使附己說以證。

translations.literal: In Huang Dehe's false accusation that Liu Ping surrendered to the enemy, he bribed Ping's slave with a gold belt to attach himself to Dehe's account as proof.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Dehe falsely accused Liu Ping of surrendering to the enemy, he bribed Ping's slave with a gold belt to support his story.

sentences.zh: 平家二百口皆械繫。

translations.literal: Ping's household of two hundred persons were all shackled and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Ping's household of two hundred persons were all shackled and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 詔彥博置獄於河中，鞫治得實。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yanbo to set up a court at Hezhong; investigation established the truth.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Yanbo to set up a court at Hezhong; investigation established the truth.

sentences.zh: 德和黨援盛，謀翻其獄，至遣他御史來。

translations.literal: Dehe's factional support was strong and they plotted to overturn the case, even sending another censor.
translations.idiomatic: Dehe's faction was powerful and plotted to overturn the verdict, even sending another censor.

sentences.zh: 彥博拒不納，曰：「朝廷慮獄不就，故遣君。

translations.literal: Yanbo refused to accept him and said: "The court feared the case would not succeed, and therefore sent you.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo refused to accept him and said, "The court feared the case would fail, and therefore sent you.

sentences.zh: 今案具矣，宜亟還，事或弗成，彥博執其咎。」

translations.literal: Now the case is complete—you should return at once; if matters fail, Yanbo will bear the blame."
translations.idiomatic: The case is complete now—you should return at once; if anything goes wrong, Yanbo will bear the blame."

sentences.zh: 德和並奴卒就誅。

translations.literal: Dehe together with the slave were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Dehe and the slave were executed.

sentences.zh: 以直史館為河東轉運副使。

translations.literal: As Compiler at the Historiography Office he became Vice Transport Commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: As compiler at the Historiography Office he became vice transport commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 麟州餉道回遠，銀城河外有唐時故道，廢弗治，彥博父洎為轉運使日，將復之，未及而卒。

translations.literal: The supply route to Linzhou was circuitous and distant; beyond Yincheng River there was an old Tang-era road abandoned and unrepaired; when Yanbo's father Ji was transport commissioner he was about to restore it but died before completing it.
translations.idiomatic: The supply route to Linzhou was long and circuitous; beyond Yincheng River lay an old Tang road that had been abandoned; when Yanbo's father Ji was transport commissioner he had planned to restore it but died before finishing.

sentences.zh: 彥博嗣成父志，益儲粟。

translations.literal: Yanbo succeeded in fulfilling his father's intent and further stored grain.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo fulfilled his father's intent and stored more grain.

sentences.zh: 元昊來寇，圍城十日，知有備，解去。

translations.literal: When Yuanhao came to raid, he besieged the city ten days, saw there were preparations, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanhao invaded, he besieged the city for ten days, saw that it was prepared, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 遷天章閣待制、都轉運使，連進龍圖閣、樞密直學士、知秦州，改益州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin Academician Awaiting Orders at the Tianzhang Pavilion and Overall Transport Commissioner, successively advanced to Dragon Diagram Hall, Academician Expositor-in-ordinary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and administrator of Qinzhou, then changed to Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hanlin academician awaiting orders at the Tianzhang Pavilion and overall transport commissioner, then successively promoted to the Dragon Diagram Hall, expositor-academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and administrator of Qinzhou, and later transferred to Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗擊球鈐轄廨，聞外喧甚，乃卒長杖一卒，不伏。

translations.literal: Once while playing ball at the supervisory commissioner's office he heard great clamor outside—a company commander was beating a soldier who would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Once while playing ball at the supervisory commissioner's office he heard a great uproar outside—a company commander was beating a soldier who refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 呼入問狀，令引出與杖，又不受，復呼入斬之，竟球乃歸。

translations.literal: He summoned him in to ask the facts, ordered him led out for beating, and again he would not submit; he summoned him in again and beheaded him, then finished the game and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the man in to question him, ordered him led out for beating, and when he still refused, summoned him in again and beheaded him; only then did he finish the game and return.

sentences.zh: 召拜樞密副使、參知政事。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Associate Chief Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and associate chief councillor.

sentences.zh: 貝州王則反，明鎬討之，久不克。

translations.literal: Wang Ze rebelled at Beizhou; Ming Hao campaigned against him but long could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ze rebelled at Beizhou; Ming Hao campaigned against him but could not defeat him for a long time.

sentences.zh: 彥博請行，命為宣撫使，旬日賊潰，檻則送京師。

translations.literal: Yanbo requested to go; he was appointed pacification commissioner, and within ten days the rebels collapsed; Ze was caged and sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo asked to go; he was appointed pacification commissioner, and within ten days the rebels collapsed; Ze was caged and sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 拜同中書門下平章事、集賢殿大學士。

translations.literal: He was appointed Associate Chief Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery and Grand Academician of the Hall for Assembling the Worthy.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed associate chief councillor and grand academician of the Hall for Assembling the Worthy.

sentences.zh: 薦張環、韓維、王安石等恬退守道，乞褒勸以厲風俗。

translations.literal: He recommended Zhang Huan, Han Wei, Wang Anshi, and others as tranquil in withdrawal and steadfast in the Way, begging that they be praised and encouraged to sharpen custom.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Zhang Huan, Han Wei, Wang Anshi, and others as men of quiet integrity and begged that they be praised and encouraged to sharpen public morals.

sentences.zh: 與樞密使龐籍議省兵，凡汰為民及給半廩者合八萬，論者紛然，謂必聚為盜，帝亦疑焉。

translations.literal: With Military Affairs Commissioner Pang Ji he deliberated reducing troops; those demobilized as civilians and those given half stipend totaled eighty thousand; debaters were in uproar, saying they would surely gather as bandits, and the emperor also doubted.
translations.idiomatic: With military affairs commissioner Pang Ji he planned to reduce the army; those demobilized as civilians and those given half stipends totaled eighty thousand; critics protested that they would surely become bandits, and the emperor also had doubts.

sentences.zh: 彥博曰：「今公私困竭，正坐兵冗。

translations.literal: Yanbo said: "Now public and private are exhausted and drained—this is precisely because troops are redundant.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo said, "Public and private resources are exhausted precisely because the army is bloated.

sentences.zh: 脫有難，臣請死之。」

translations.literal: If difficulty arises, your servant asks to die for it."
translations.idiomatic: If trouble arises, I ask to answer for it with my life."

sentences.zh: 其策訖行，歸兵亦無事。

translations.literal: The policy was carried through to completion, and the demobilized troops also had no incident.
translations.idiomatic: The policy was carried out, and the demobilized troops caused no trouble.

sentences.zh: 進昭文館大學士。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Academician of the Hall of Brilliance in Literature.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to grand academician of the Hall of Brilliance in Literature.

sentences.zh: 御史唐介劾其在蜀日以奇錦結宮掖，因之登用。

translations.literal: Censor Tang Jie impeached him for using rare brocades in Shu days to win the palace inner quarters and thereby gain appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Tang Jie impeached him for using rare brocades while in Shu to win favor in the inner palace and thereby gain promotion.

sentences.zh: 介既貶，彥博亦罷為觀文殿大學士、知許州，改忠武軍節度使、知永興軍。

translations.literal: After Jie was demoted, Yanbo was also dismissed as Academician of the Hall for Viewing Culture and administrator of Xuzhou, then changed to Military Commissioner of the Zhongwu army and administrator of the Yongxing army.
translations.idiomatic: After Jie was demoted, Yanbo was also dismissed as academician of the Hall for Viewing Culture and administrator of Xuzhou, then made military commissioner of the Zhongwu army and administrator of the Yongxing army.

sentences.zh: 至和二年，復以吏部尚書同中書門下平章事、昭文館大學士，與富弼同拜，士大夫皆以得人為慶，語見《弼傳》。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhihe he was again made Minister of Personnel, Associate Chief Councillor, and Grand Academician of the Hall of Brilliance in Literature, appointed together with Fu Bi; scholar-officials all celebrated that the right men had been obtained—as told in the Biography of Bi.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhihe 2 (1055) he was again made minister of personnel, associate chief councillor, and grand academician of the Hall of Brilliance in Literature, appointed on the same day as Fu Bi; scholar-officials celebrated that the right men had been chosen—the account is in Bi's biography.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，帝方受朝，疾暴作，扶入禁中。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, as the emperor was receiving court, illness suddenly seized him and he was supported into the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year, as the emperor was holding court, he was suddenly stricken with illness and helped into the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 彥博呼內侍史志聰問狀，對曰：「禁密不敢漏言。」

translations.literal: Yanbo summoned the inner attendant Shi Zhicong to ask his condition; he replied: "It is forbidden and secret—I dare not leak word."
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo summoned the inner attendant Shi Zhicong to ask after the emperor's condition; he replied, "It is forbidden and secret—I dare not speak of it."

sentences.zh: 彥博叱之曰：「爾曹出入禁闥，不令宰相知天子起居，欲何為邪？

translations.literal: Yanbo rebuked him: "You people go in and out of the forbidden gates yet do not let the chief councillors know the Son of Heaven's daily life—what do you intend?
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo rebuked him, "You go in and out of the forbidden gates yet keep the chief ministers ignorant of the Son of Heaven's condition—what do you intend?

sentences.zh: 自今疾勢增損必以告，不爾，當行軍法。」

translations.literal: From now on whether the illness worsens or improves you must report it—otherwise military law will be applied."
translations.idiomatic: From now on you must report whether his condition worsens or improves—otherwise you will face military law."

sentences.zh: 又與同列劉沆、富弼謀啟醮大慶殿，因留宿殿廬。

translations.literal: He also with his colleagues Liu Hang and Fu Bi planned to open a ritual at the Great Celebration Hall and thereby lodged overnight in the hall quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He also planned with his colleagues Liu Hang and Fu Bi to perform a ritual at the Great Celebration Hall and lodged overnight in the hall quarters.

sentences.zh: 志聰曰：「無故事。」

translations.literal: Zhicong said: "There is no precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Zhicong said, "There is no precedent."

sentences.zh: 彥博曰：「此豈論故事時邪？」

translations.literal: Yanbo said: "Is this a time to discuss precedent?"
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo said, "Is this a time to discuss precedent?"

sentences.zh: 知開封府王素夜叩宮門上變，不使入；

translations.literal: The Kaifeng administrator Wang Su knocked at the palace gate at night to report an emergency and was not admitted;
translations.idiomatic: The Kaifeng administrator Wang Su knocked at the palace gate at night to report an emergency and was not admitted;

sentences.zh: 明旦言，有禁卒告都虞候欲為亂。

translations.literal: the next morning he reported that a palace guardsman had accused the company commander of plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: the next morning he reported that a palace guardsman had accused the company commander of plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 沆欲捕治，彥博召都指揮使許懷德，問都虞候何如人，懷德稱其願可保。

translations.literal: Hang wished to arrest and try him; Yanbo summoned the overall commander Xu Huaide and asked what sort of man the company commander was—Huaide said he was honest and could be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Hang wished to arrest and try him; Yanbo summoned the overall commander Xu Huaide and asked what sort of man the company commander was—Huaide said he was honest and could be trusted.

sentences.zh: 彥博曰：「然則卒有怨，誣之耳。

translations.literal: Yanbo said: "Then the guardsman bears a grudge and has falsely accused him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo said, "Then the guardsman bears a grudge and has falsely accused him.

sentences.zh: 當亟誅之以靖眾。」

translations.literal: He should be swiftly executed to quiet the multitude."
translations.idiomatic: The accuser should be executed at once to quiet the troops."

sentences.zh: 乃請沆判狀尾，斬於軍門。

translations.literal: He then asked Hang to endorse the report at the end, and he was beheaded at the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked Hang to endorse the report, and the accuser was beheaded at the army gate.

sentences.zh: 先是，弼用朝士李仲昌策，自澶州商胡河穿六漯渠，入橫壠故道。

translations.literal: Earlier, Bi had used the court scholar Li Zhongchang's plan to cut from the Shanghu River at Dazhou through the Six Luo channels into the old course of Henglong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Bi had adopted court scholar Li Zhongchang's plan to cut a canal from the Shanghu River at Dazhou through the Six Luo channels into the old Henglong course.

sentences.zh: 北京留守賈昌朝素惡弼，陰約內侍武繼隆，令司天官二人俟執政聚時，於殿庭抗言國家不當穿河於北方，致上體不安。

translations.literal: The Beijing garrison commander Jia Changchao had long hated Bi and secretly arranged with the inner attendant Wu Jilong to have two astronomical officials, when the chief administrators gathered, speak out boldly in the court hall that the state ought not cut a canal in the north, causing the sovereign's person to be unwell.
translations.idiomatic: The Beijing garrison commander Jia Changchao had long hated Bi and secretly arranged with the inner attendant Wu Jilong to have two astronomical officials, when the chief administrators gathered, declare in court that the state ought not cut a canal in the north, lest the sovereign's health suffer.

sentences.zh: 彥博知其意有所在，然未有以制之，後數日，二人又上言，請皇后同聽政，亦繼隆所教也。

translations.literal: Yanbo knew their intent had a source but had no means to control it; several days later the two again submitted statements asking that the empress jointly hear government—this too was what Jilong had taught.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo knew their statements had a hidden source but had no means to stop it; several days later the two again memorialized asking that the empress jointly hear government—this too was Jilong's doing.

sentences.zh: 史志聰以其狀白執政。

translations.literal: Shi Zhicong reported their statements to the chief administrators.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhicong reported their statements to the chief administrators.

sentences.zh: 彥博視而懷之，不以示同列，而有喜色，徐召二人詰之曰：「汝今日有所言乎？」

translations.literal: Yanbo looked and kept it in his bosom, not showing his colleagues, yet with a pleased expression; he slowly summoned the two and questioned them: "Did you have something to say today?"
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo read it and kept it to himself without showing his colleagues, yet with a pleased expression; he slowly summoned the two and asked, "Did you have something to say today?"

translations.literal: They said: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: They said, "Yes."

sentences.zh: 彥博曰：「天文變異，汝職所當言也。

translations.literal: Yanbo said: "Celestial anomalies are what your office should speak of.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo said, "Celestial anomalies are what your office should report.

sentences.zh: 何得輒預國家大事？

translations.literal: How dare you rashly intervene in great affairs of state?
translations.idiomatic: How dare you intervene in great affairs of state?

sentences.zh: 汝罪當族！」

translations.literal: Your crime deserves extermination of the clan!"
translations.idiomatic: Your crime deserves the extermination of your clan!"

sentences.zh: 二人懼，色變。

translations.literal: The two were afraid and their color changed.
translations.idiomatic: The two were terrified and turned pale.

sentences.zh: 彥博曰：「觀汝直狂愚耳，未忍治汝罪，自今無得復然。」

translations.literal: Yanbo said: "Seeing you are plainly mad and foolish, I cannot bear to punish your crime—from now on you must not do so again."
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo said, "You are plainly mad and foolish; I cannot bear to punish you—do not do this again."

sentences.zh: 二人退，乃出狀示同列。

translations.literal: When the two withdrew, he then produced the statements and showed his colleagues.
translations.idiomatic: When the two withdrew, he produced the statements and showed his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 同列皆憤怒曰：「奴敢爾僭言，何不斬之？」

translations.literal: His colleagues were all angry and said: "How dare slaves speak so presumptuously—why not behead them?"
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues were all angry and said, "How dare these men speak so presumptuously—why not behead them?"

sentences.zh: 彥博曰：「斬之，則事彰灼，於中宮不安。」

translations.literal: Yanbo said: "If we behead them, the matter will blaze forth and the inner palace will be unsettled."
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo said, "If we behead them, the matter will blaze forth and the inner palace will be unsettled."

sentences.zh: 眾皆曰：「善。」

translations.literal: All said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: All said, "Good."

sentences.zh: 既而議遣司天官定六漯方位，復使二人往。

translations.literal: Soon after they deliberated sending astronomical officials to fix the Six Luo positions and again sent the two.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after they decided to send astronomical officials to fix the Six Luo positions and again sent the two men.

sentences.zh: 繼隆白請留之，彥博曰：「彼本不敢妄言，有教之者耳。」

translations.literal: Jilong reported asking to retain them; Yanbo said: "They originally did not dare speak rashly—someone taught them, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Jilong asked to keep them; Yanbo said, "They did not dare speak rashly on their own—someone taught them, that is all."

sentences.zh: 繼隆默不敢對。

translations.literal: Jilong was silent and did not dare reply.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong was silent and did not dare reply.

sentences.zh: 二人至六漯，恐治前罪，更言六漯在東北，非正北也。

translations.literal: When the two reached the Six Luo, fearing punishment for their earlier crime, they further said the Six Luo lay in the northeast, not due north.
translations.idiomatic: When the two reached the Six Luo, fearing punishment for their earlier offense, they said the Six Luo lay in the northeast, not due north.

sentences.zh: 帝疾愈，彥博等始歸第。

translations.literal: When the emperor's illness improved, Yanbo and the others at last returned to their residences.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor recovered, Yanbo and the others at last returned home.

sentences.zh: 當是時，京師業業，賴彥博、弼持重，眾心以安。

translations.literal: At that time the capital was fearful and uneasy; relying on Yanbo and Bi's weightiness, popular hearts were calmed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the capital was fearful and uneasy; relying on Yanbo and Bi's steady authority, the people's hearts were calmed.

sentences.zh: 沆密白帝曰：「陛下違豫時，彥博擅斬告反者。」

translations.literal: Hang secretly reported to the emperor: "When Your Majesty was ill, Yanbo on his own authority beheaded the one who reported rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: Hang secretly reported to the emperor, "When Your Majesty was ill, Yanbo on his own authority beheaded the man who reported a plot."

sentences.zh: 彥博聞之，以沆判呈，帝意乃解。

translations.literal: When Yanbo heard of it he presented Hang's endorsement, and the emperor's mind was thereupon relieved.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanbo heard of this he presented Hang's endorsement, and the emperor's suspicions were cleared.

sentences.zh: 御史吳中復乞召還唐介。

translations.literal: Censor Wu Zhongfu begged to recall Tang Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wu Zhongfu memorialized to recall Tang Jie.

sentences.zh: 彥博因言，介頃為御史，言臣事多中臣病，其間雖有風聞之誤，然當時責之太深，請如中復奏。

translations.literal: Yanbo thereupon said: "Jie was recently censor; in speaking of my affairs he often hit my faults; though among them there were errors of rumor, yet at the time he was punished too deeply—I beg that it follow Zhongfu's memorial."
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo said, "Jie was recently censor; in criticizing me he often struck home, and though some charges rested on rumor, he was punished too harshly—I beg that Your Majesty follow Zhongfu's memorial."

sentences.zh: 時以彥博為厚德。

translations.literal: At the time Yanbo was regarded as deeply virtuous.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yanbo was regarded as a man of deep virtue.

sentences.zh: 久之，以河陽三城節度使同平章事、判河南府，封潞國公，改鎮保平、判大名府。

translations.literal: After a long while he was made Military Commissioner of the Heyang Three Cities, Associate Chief Councillor, and concurrent administrator of Henan prefecture, enfeoffed as Duke of Lu, then transferred to garrison Baoping and administer Daming prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was made military commissioner of the Heyang Three Cities, associate chief councillor, and concurrent administrator of Henan, enfeoffed as Duke of Lu, then transferred to garrison Baoping and administer Daming.

sentences.zh: 又改鎮成德，遷尚書左僕射、判太原府。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to garrison Chengde, promoted to Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and concurrent administrator of Taiyuan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was again transferred to garrison Chengde, promoted to left vice director of the Imperial Secretariat, and made concurrent administrator of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 俄復鎮保平、判河南。

translations.literal: Soon he again garrisoned Baoping and administered Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he again garrisoned Baoping and administered Henan.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，英宗即位，起復成德軍節度使，三上表乞終喪，許之。

translations.literal: On mourning for his mother, when Emperor Yingzong ascended he was recalled from mourning as Military Commissioner of the Chengde army; he submitted three memorials begging to complete mourning, and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When he mourned his mother, Yingzong on ascending recalled him from mourning as military commissioner of the Chengde army; he submitted three memorials begging to complete mourning, and was granted permission.

sentences.zh: 初，仁宗之不豫也，彥博與富弼等乞立儲嗣。

translations.literal: Early on, when Emperor Renzong was ill, Yanbo with Fu Bi and others begged to establish an heir.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, when Emperor Renzong fell ill, Yanbo with Fu Bi and others begged to establish an heir.

sentences.zh: 仁宗許焉，而後宮將有就館者，故其事緩。

translations.literal: Renzong assented, but the inner palace was about to have someone enter the birthing lodge, and therefore the matter was delayed.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong assented, but a consort in the inner palace was about to give birth, and so the matter was delayed.

sentences.zh: 已而彥博去位，其後弼亦以憂去。

translations.literal: Before long Yanbo left office; afterward Bi also left on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yanbo left office; afterward Bi also left on account of mourning.

sentences.zh: 彥博既服闋，復以故官判河南，有詔入覲。

translations.literal: When Yanbo had completed mourning he again took his former post administering Henan, and an edict ordered him to attend audience.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanbo had completed mourning he resumed his former post administering Henan, and an edict ordered him to attend audience.

sentences.zh: 英宗曰：「朕之立，卿之力也。」

translations.literal: Yingzong said: "My establishment was your strength."
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong said, "My accession was your doing."

sentences.zh: 彥博竦然對曰：「陛下入繼大統，乃先帝聖意，皇太后協贊之力，臣何聞力之有？

translations.literal: Yanbo started in alarm and replied: "Your Majesty's entering to succeed the great succession was the late emperor's sagely intent and the empress dowager's power of joint support—what strength had your servant heard of?
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo started in alarm and replied, "Your Majesty's succession was the late emperor's sagely intent and the empress dowager's support—what strength had I in it?

sentences.zh: 兼陛下登儲纂極之時，臣方在外，皆韓琦等承聖志受顧命，臣無與焉。」

translations.literal: Moreover when Your Majesty was established as heir and ascended the pinnacle, your servant was still abroad—all was Han Qi and others receiving the sagely will and the dying charge; your servant had no part."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover when Your Majesty was named heir and ascended the throne, I was still abroad—it was Han Qi and others who received the late emperor's charge; I had no part in it."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「備聞始議，卿於朕有恩。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I have fully heard of the initial deliberation—you have shown me favor."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have heard of the early deliberations—you showed me favor."

sentences.zh: 彥博遜避不敢當。

translations.literal: Yanbo modestly declined and did not dare accept.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo modestly declined and would not accept the credit.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「暫煩西行，即召還矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "For the moment we trouble you to go west—you will be recalled soon."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "For the moment we trouble you to go west—you will be recalled soon."

sentences.zh: 尋除侍中，徙鎮淮南、判永興軍，入為樞密使、劍南西川節度使。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Palace Attendant, transferred to garrison Huainan and administer the Yongxing army, and entered as Military Affairs Commissioner and Military Commissioner of the Jiannan West circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed palace attendant, transferred to garrison Huainan and administer the Yongxing army, and entered court as military affairs commissioner and military commissioner of the Jiannan West circuit.

sentences.zh: 熙寧二年，相陳升之，詔：「彥博朝廷宗臣，其令升之位彥博下，以稱遇賢之意。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Xining, Chen Shengzhi was made chief councillor; an edict said: "Yanbo is a dynastic elder of the court—let Shengzhi's rank be below Yanbo, to accord with honoring the worthy."
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 2 (1069), Chen Shengzhi was made chief councillor; an edict said, "Yanbo is a dynastic elder of the court—let Shengzhi's rank be below Yanbo, to honor the worthy."

sentences.zh: 彥博曰：「國朝樞密使，無位宰相上者，獨曹利用嘗在王曾、張知白上。

translations.literal: Yanbo said: "In our dynasty's Military Affairs Commissioners, none has ranked above the chief councillor except Cao Liyong, who once ranked above Wang Zeng and Zhang Zhibai.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo said, "In our dynasty no military affairs commissioner has ranked above the chief councillor except Cao Liyong, who once ranked above Wang Zeng and Zhang Zhibai.

sentences.zh: 臣忝知禮義，不敢效利用所為，以紊朝著。」

translations.literal: Your servant is shamed to know ritual and righteousness and does not dare imitate what Liyong did, to disorder court regulations."
translations.idiomatic: I am shamed to know ritual and righteousness and dare not imitate Liyong's conduct and disorder court regulations."

sentences.zh: 固辭乃止。

translations.literal: He firmly declined and it then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 夏人犯大順，慶帥李復圭以陳圖方略授鈐轄李信等，趣使出戰。

translations.literal: The Tangut violated Dashun; the Qingzhou commander Li Fugui gave Chen Tu's stratagem to Supervisory Commissioner Li Xin and others and urged them to go out and fight.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut attacked Dashun; the Qingzhou commander Li Fugui gave Chen Tu's battle plan to supervisory commissioner Li Xin and others and urged them into battle.

sentences.zh: 及敗，乃妄奏信罪。

translations.literal: When they were defeated, he then falsely memorialized Xin's crime.
translations.idiomatic: When they were defeated, he falsely memorialized that Xin was to blame.

sentences.zh: 彥博暴其非，宰相王安石曲誅信等，秦人冤之。

translations.literal: Yanbo exposed his wrong; Chief Councillor Wang Anshi bent the law to execute Xin and others—the people of Qin regarded it as injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo exposed the injustice; chief councillor Wang Anshi bent the law to execute Xin and others—the people of Qin regarded it as a grievous wrong.

sentences.zh: 慶州兵亂，彥博言於帝曰：「朝廷行事，務合人心，宜兼採眾論，以靜重為先。

translations.literal: When Qingzhou troops mutinied, Yanbo said to the emperor: "In court actions, the task is to accord with popular hearts—it is fitting to take many opinions together and put calm weightiness first.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingzhou troops mutinied, Yanbo said to the emperor, "The court's actions must accord with the people's hearts; it should heed many opinions and put calm steadiness first.

sentences.zh: 陛下厲精求治，而人心未安，蓋更張之過也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty strives with vigor to seek good governance, yet popular hearts are not at ease—this is likely the fault of sweeping change.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty strives for good governance, yet the people's hearts are not at ease—this is likely the fault of sweeping change.

sentences.zh: 祖宗法未必皆不可行，但有偏而不舉之敝爾。」

translations.literal: The laws of the ancestors are not necessarily all unworkable—there is only the flaw of partiality and not carrying them through."
translations.idiomatic: The laws of the ancestors are not necessarily all unworkable—there is only the flaw of enforcing them selectively."

sentences.zh: 安石知為己發，奮然排之曰：「求去民害，何為不可？

translations.literal: Anshi knew this was aimed at him and vehemently rebutted: "Seeking to remove harm to the people—why may it not be done?
translations.idiomatic: Anshi knew this was aimed at him and vehemently rebutted, "Seeking to remove harm to the people—why may that not be done?

sentences.zh: 若萬事隳脞，乃西晉之風，何益於治？」

translations.literal: If every matter is chipped and broken, that is the style of Western Jin—what benefit is there to governance?"
translations.idiomatic: If every matter is chipped away in petty caution, that is the style of Western Jin—what benefit is there to governance?"

sentences.zh: 御史張商英欲附安石，摭樞密使他事以搖彥博，坐不實貶。

translations.literal: Censor Zhang Shangying wished to attach himself to Anshi and gathered other matters of the Bureau of Military Affairs to shake Yanbo; on finding them untrue he was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhang Shangying wished to attach himself to Anshi and gathered other charges against the Bureau of Military Affairs to shake Yanbo; when they proved false he was demoted.

sentences.zh: 彥博在樞府九年，又以極論市易司監賣果實，損國體斂民怨，為安石所惡，力引去。

translations.literal: Yanbo was in the Bureau of Military Affairs nine years; he also argued forcefully that the Market Exchange Office's supervised sale of fruit harmed state dignity and gathered popular resentment, was hated by Anshi, and forcefully sought to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo served in the Bureau of Military Affairs nine years; he also argued forcefully that the Market Exchange Office's monopoly on fruit harmed state dignity and stirred popular resentment, was hated by Anshi, and forcefully sought to leave.

sentences.zh: 拜司空、河東節度使、判河陽，徙大名府。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of Works, Military Commissioner of Hedong, and concurrent administrator of Heyang, then transferred to Daming prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed minister of works, military commissioner of Hedong, and concurrent administrator of Heyang, then transferred to Daming.

sentences.zh: 身雖在外，而帝眷有加。

translations.literal: Though his person was outside, the emperor's favor toward him increased.
translations.idiomatic: Though he served outside the capital, the emperor's favor toward him only increased.

sentences.zh: 時監司多新進少年，轉運判官汪輔之輒奏彥博不事事，帝批其奏以付彥博曰：「以侍中舊德，故煩臥護北門，細務不必勞心。

translations.literal: At the time many supervisory officials were newly advanced youths; transport vice commissioner Wang Fuzhi promptly memorialized that Yanbo did not attend to affairs; the emperor annotated his memorial and sent it to Yanbo, saying: "Because of the old virtue of the Palace Attendant, we trouble you to lie and guard the northern gate—minor matters need not weary your mind.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many supervisory officials were newly advanced youths; transport vice commissioner Wang Fuzhi memorialized that Yanbo neglected his duties; the emperor annotated the memorial and sent it to Yanbo, saying, "Because of your long-standing virtue as palace attendant, we trouble you to guard the northern gate in repose—minor matters need not weary your mind.

sentences.zh: 輔之小臣，敢爾無禮，將別有處置。」

translations.literal: Fuzhi is a petty official who dares such rudeness—he will receive separate disposition."
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhi is a petty official who dares such rudeness—he will be dealt with separately."

sentences.zh: 未幾，罷去。

translations.literal: Before long he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Fuzhi was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 初，選人有李公義者，請以鐵龍爪治河，宦者黃懷信沿其制為濬川杷，天下指笑以為兒戲，安石獨信之，遣都水丞范子淵行其法。

translations.literal: Early on, a candidate named Li Gongyi requested using iron dragon claws to control the river; the eunuch Huang Huaixin followed his design to make a river-dredging rake; the empire pointed and laughed, taking it as child's play—Anshi alone trusted it and sent Director of Waterways Fan Ziyuan to carry out the method.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, a candidate named Li Gongyi proposed using iron dragon claws to control the river; the eunuch Huang Huaixin adapted the design into a river-dredging rake; the empire laughed at it as child's play—Anshi alone trusted it and sent director of waterways Fan Ziyuan to carry out the method.

sentences.zh: 子淵奏用杷之功，水悉歸故道，退出民田數萬頃。

translations.literal: Ziyuan memorialized the rake's achievement—the water all returned to the old course and tens of thousands of qing of civilian fields were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyuan memorialized the rake's success—the water all returned to the old course and tens of thousands of qing of civilian fields were restored.

sentences.zh: 詔大名核實，彥博言：「河非杷可濬，雖甚愚之人，皆知無益，臣不敢雷同罔上。」

translations.literal: An edict ordered Daming to verify; Yanbo said: "The river cannot be dredged by rake—even the most foolish person knows it is useless—your servant does not dare echo in falsehood above."
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Daming to verify; Yanbo said, "The river cannot be dredged with a rake—even the most foolish person knows it is useless—I dare not echo falsehood to the throne."

sentences.zh: 疏至，帝不悅，復遣知制誥熊本等行視，如彥博言。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived the emperor was displeased and again sent Drafting Official Xiong Ben and others to inspect on site—as Yanbo had said.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived the emperor was displeased and again sent drafting official Xiong Ben and others to inspect on site—as Yanbo had said.

sentences.zh: 子淵乃請覲，言本等見安石罷，意彥博復相，故傅會其說。

translations.literal: Ziyuan then requested audience, saying Ben and the others saw Anshi dismissed and thought Yanbo would again be chief councillor, and therefore attached themselves to his account.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyuan then requested audience, saying Ben and the others saw Anshi dismissed and thought Yanbo would again be chief councillor, and therefore sided with his account.

sentences.zh: 御史蔡確亦論本奉使無狀。

translations.literal: Censor Cai Que also argued that Ben's mission conduct was unseemly.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Cai Que also argued that Ben's conduct on the mission was unseemly.

sentences.zh: 本等皆得罪，獨彥博勿問。

translations.literal: Ben and the others were all punished; Yanbo alone was not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Ben and the others were all punished; Yanbo alone was not questioned.

sentences.zh: 尋加司徒。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the additional title Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was given the additional title minister of education.

sentences.zh: 元豐三年，拜太尉，復判河南。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanfeng he was appointed Grand Guardian and again administered Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanfeng (1080) he was appointed grand guardian and again administered Henan.

sentences.zh: 於是王同老言至和中議儲嗣事，彥博適入朝，神宗問之，彥博以前對英宗者復於帝曰：「先帝天命所在，神器有歸，實仁祖知子之明，慈聖擁佑之力，臣等何功？」

translations.literal: Thereupon Wang Tonglao spoke of the Zhihe deliberation on establishing an heir; Yanbo happened to enter court; Shenzong questioned him; Yanbo repeated to the emperor what he had earlier replied to Yingzong: "The late emperor's mandate of Heaven was fixed, the sacred vessel had its destination—it was truly Renzu's wisdom in knowing his son and Cisheng's power of support and protection—what merit had your servants?"
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Wang Tonglao spoke of the Zhihe deliberation on establishing an heir; Yanbo happened to enter court; Shenzong questioned him; Yanbo repeated to the emperor what he had earlier told Yingzong: "The late emperor's mandate of Heaven was fixed and the sacred vessel had its destination—it was truly Renzong's wisdom in knowing his son and the empress dowager's power of support—what merit had we?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「雖云天命，亦繫人謀。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Though it is called Heaven's mandate, it also depends on human design.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Though it is called Heaven's mandate, it also depends on human design.

sentences.zh: 卿深厚不伐善，陰德如丙吉，真定策社稷臣也。」

translations.literal: You are deep and weighty and do not boast of good deeds; hidden virtue like Bing Ji—you are truly a minister who settled the policy of state and altars."
translations.idiomatic: You are deep and weighty and do not boast of your deeds; your hidden virtue is like Bing Ji's—you are truly a minister who settled the succession."

sentences.zh: 彥博曰：「如周勃、霍光，是為定策。

translations.literal: Yanbo said: "Like Zhou Bo and Huo Guang—that is called settling the policy.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo said, "Men like Zhou Bo and Huo Guang—that is what is called settling the succession.

sentences.zh: 自至和以來，中外之臣獻言甚眾，臣等雖嘗有請，弗果行。

translations.literal: From Zhihe onward, ministers inside and outside offered many words; your servants though once made requests, they were not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhihe onward many ministers offered advice; we too once made requests, but they were not carried out.

sentences.zh: 其後韓琦等訖就大事，蓋琦功也。」

translations.literal: Afterward Han Qi and others at last accomplished the great affair—this was Qi's merit."
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Han Qi and others at last accomplished the great affair—that was Qi's merit."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「發端為難，是時仁祖意已定，嘉祐之末，止申前詔爾。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "To begin is the hard part; at that time Renzu's intent was already fixed—in the last years of Jiayou it was only reiterating the earlier edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "To begin is the hard part; at that time Renzong's intent was already fixed—in the last years of Jiayou it was only reiterating the earlier edict.

sentences.zh: 正如丙吉、霍光，不相掩也。」

translations.literal: Just as with Bing Ji and Huo Guang, they do not obscure one another."
translations.idiomatic: Just as with Bing Ji and Huo Guang, their merits do not obscure one another."

sentences.zh: 遂加彥博兩鎮節度使，辭不拜。

translations.literal: He thereupon added for Yanbo two military commissioner posts; Yanbo declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon offered Yanbo two additional military commissioner posts; Yanbo declined.

sentences.zh: 將行，賜宴瓊林苑，兩遣中謁者遺詩祖道，當世榮之。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, a banquet was granted at the Qionglin Garden; twice palace ushers were sent with poems to bid farewell on the road—the age honored it.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to depart, a banquet was granted at the Qionglin Garden; twice palace ushers were sent with poems to bid him farewell on the road—the age regarded it as a great honor.

sentences.zh: 王中正經制邊事，所過稱受密旨募禁兵，將之而西。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongzheng directed frontier affairs; wherever he passed he claimed to have received secret instructions to recruit palace guards and was taking them west.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongzheng directed frontier affairs; wherever he passed he claimed secret instructions to recruit palace guards and was taking them west.

sentences.zh: 彥博以無詔拒之，中正亦不敢募而去。

translations.literal: Yanbo refused on the grounds there was no edict; Zhongzheng also did not dare recruit and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo refused on the grounds there was no edict; Zhongzheng also did not dare recruit and departed.

sentences.zh: 久之，請老，以太師致仕，居洛陽。

translations.literal: After a long while he requested retirement on account of age, retired as Grand Preceptor, and dwelt in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he requested retirement on account of age, retired as grand preceptor, and dwelt in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，司馬光薦彥博宿德元老，宜起以自輔。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou, Sima Guang recommended Yanbo as an elder of long virtue who should be raised to assist himself.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanyou, Sima Guang recommended Yanbo as an elder of long virtue who should be raised to assist the court.

sentences.zh: 宣仁后將用為三省長官，而言事者以為不可，及命平章軍國重事，六日一朝，一月兩赴經筵，恩禮甚渥。

translations.literal: Empress Xuanren was about to use him as head of the Three Departments, but remonstrators held it impossible; he was then ordered to oversee the weighty affairs of state and army, attend court every six days, and go twice a month to the classics lecture—the favor and courtesy were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xuanren was about to make him head of the Three Departments, but remonstrators objected; he was then ordered to oversee weighty affairs of state and army, attend court every six days, and go twice a month to the classics lecture—the favor shown him was very generous.

sentences.zh: 然彥博無歲不求退，居五年，復致仕。

translations.literal: Yet Yanbo every year without fail sought to withdraw; after five years he again retired.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yanbo every year sought to withdraw; after five years he retired again.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，章惇秉政，言者論彥博朋附司馬光，詆毀先烈，降太子少保。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaosheng, Zhang Dun held power; remonstrators argued Yanbo had cliqued with Sima Guang and slandered the former worthies—he was demoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shaosheng, Zhang Dun held power; remonstrators argued Yanbo had cliqued with Sima Guang and slandered the former worthies—he was demoted to junior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，年九十二。

translations.literal: He died, aged ninety-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died, aged ninety-two.

sentences.zh: 崇寧中，預元祐黨籍。

translations.literal: During Chongning he was entered on the Yuanyou faction register.
translations.idiomatic: During Chongning he was entered on the Yuanyou faction register.

sentences.zh: 後特命出籍，追復太師，諡曰忠烈。

translations.literal: Later by special order he was removed from the register, posthumously restored as Grand Preceptor, and given the posthumous title Zhonglie (Loyal and Ardent).
translations.idiomatic: Later by special order he was removed from the register, posthumously restored as grand preceptor, and given the posthumous title Loyal and Ardent.

sentences.zh: 彥博逮事四朝，任將相五十年，名聞四夷。

translations.literal: Yanbo served four reigns, held general and councillor posts fifty years, and his name was heard among the four barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo served four reigns, held general and councillor posts for fifty years, and his name was known among the four barbarians.

sentences.zh: 元祐間，契丹使耶律永昌、劉霄來聘，蘇軾館客，與使入覲，望見彥博於殿門外，卻立改容曰：「此潞公也邪？」

translations.literal: During Yuanyou, Khitan envoys Yelü Yongchang and Liu Xiao came on embassy; Su Shi received them as host and entered audience with them; seeing Yanbo outside the hall gate they stepped back and changed expression, saying: "Is this the Duke of Lu?"
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanyou, Khitan envoys Yelü Yongchang and Liu Xiao came on embassy; Su Shi received them as host and entered audience with them; seeing Yanbo outside the hall gate they stepped back and changed expression, saying, "Is this the Duke of Lu?"

sentences.zh: 問其年，曰：「何壯也！？

translations.literal: They asked his age and said: "How vigorous!
translations.idiomatic: They asked his age and exclaimed, "How vigorous he still is!

sentences.zh: 軾曰：「使者見其容，未聞其語。

translations.literal: Shi said: "The envoys have seen his bearing but not yet heard his speech.
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "The envoys have seen his bearing but not yet heard his speech.

sentences.zh: 其綜理庶務，雖精練少年有不如；

translations.literal: In comprehensively ordering the myriad affairs, even skilled and practiced youths are not his equal;
translations.idiomatic: In managing the myriad affairs of state, even skilled young officials are not his equal;

sentences.zh: 其貫穿古今，雖專門名家有不逮。」

translations.literal: in penetrating past and present, even specialized masters of a school do not reach him."
translations.idiomatic: in penetrating past and present, even specialized masters do not reach him."

sentences.zh: 使者拱手曰：「天下異人也。」

translations.literal: The envoys bowed with clasped hands and said: "A rare man under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The envoys bowed with clasped hands and said, "A rare man under Heaven."

sentences.zh: 既歸洛，西羌首領溫溪心有名馬，請於邊吏，願以饋彥博，詔許之。

translations.literal: After returning to Luoyang, the Western Qiang leader Wenxixin had a famous horse and requested through frontier officials that he might present it to Yanbo—an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to Luoyang, the Western Qiang leader Wenxixin had a famous horse and requested through frontier officials that he might present it to Yanbo—an edict permitted it.

sentences.zh: 其為外國所敬如此。

translations.literal: Such was the respect shown him by foreign states.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the respect shown him by foreign states.

sentences.zh: 彥博雖窮貴極富，而平居接物謙下，尊德樂善，如恐不及。

translations.literal: Though Yanbo reached the utmost in rank and wealth, in daily life in receiving others he was humble, honoring virtue and delighting in good as if fearing he could not reach it.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yanbo reached the utmost in rank and wealth, in daily life he received others with humility, honoring virtue and delighting in good as if he could never do enough.

sentences.zh: 其在洛也，洛人邵雍、程灝兄弟皆以道自重，賓接之如布衣交。

translations.literal: When he was in Luoyang, the Luoyang men Shao Yong and the Cheng brothers Hao and Yi all took the Way as their weight; he received them as guests like commoner friends.
translations.idiomatic: When he was in Luoyang, Shao Yong and the Cheng brothers Hao and Yi all took the Way as their standard; he received them as guests like friends among commoners.

sentences.zh: 與富弼、司馬光等十三人，用白居易九老會故事，置酒賦詩相樂，序齒不序官，為堂，繪像其中，謂之「洛陽耆英會」，好事者莫不慕之。

translations.literal: With Fu Bi, Sima Guang, and twelve others he used Bai Juyi's story of the Nine Elders' gathering, set out wine and composed poetry for mutual pleasure, ordering by age not by office; they built a hall and painted portraits within, calling it the "Luoyang Gathering of Worthy Elders"—men of affairs all admired it.
translations.idiomatic: With Fu Bi, Sima Guang, and twelve others he followed Bai Juyi's Nine Elders' gathering, set out wine and composed poetry for mutual pleasure, ordering by age not by office; they built a hall and painted portraits within, calling it the Luoyang Gathering of Worthy Elders—men of affairs all admired it.

sentences.zh: 神宗導洛通汴，而主者遏絕洛水，不使入城中，洛人頗患苦之。

translations.literal: Shenzong guided the Luo to connect with the Bian, but those in charge blocked the Luo water and did not let it enter the city—the people of Luoyang were quite afflicted.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong guided the Luo River to connect with the Bian, but those in charge blocked the Luo and did not let it enter the city—the people of Luoyang suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 彥博因中使劉惟簡至洛，語其故，惟簡以聞。

translations.literal: Yanbo, because palace envoy Liu Weijian came to Luoyang, told him the reason, and Weijian reported it.
translations.idiomatic: When palace envoy Liu Weijian came to Luoyang, Yanbo told him the reason, and Weijian reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔令通行如初，遂為洛城無窮之利。

translations.literal: An edict ordered passage as before, and it then became an inexhaustible benefit for Luoyang city.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered passage restored as before, and it became an inexhaustible benefit for Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 彥博八子，皆歷要官。

translations.literal: Yanbo had eight sons, all of whom held important offices.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo had eight sons, all of whom held important offices.

sentences.zh: 第六子及甫，初以大理評事直史館，與邢恕相善。

translations.literal: The sixth son Jifu was first made Evaluator at the Court of Judicial Review and Compiler at the Historiography Office, and was on good terms with Xing Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth son Jifu was first made evaluator at the Court of Judicial Review and compiler at the Historiography Office, and was on good terms with Xing Shu.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，為吏部員外郎，以直龍圖閣知同州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou he was Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and, as Compiler at the Dragon Diagram Hall, administered Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanyou he was vice director of the Ministry of Personnel and, as compiler at the Dragon Diagram Hall, administered Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 彥博平章軍國，及甫由右司員外郎引嫌改衛尉、光祿少卿。

translations.literal: When Yanbo oversaw state and army affairs, Jifu, from Vice Director of the Right Secretariat, withdrew on grounds of conflict of interest and was changed to Vice Director of the Imperial Guard and Vice Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanbo oversaw state and army affairs, Jifu withdrew on grounds of conflict of interest from his post as vice director of the right secretariat and was made vice director of the imperial guard and vice director of the imperial household.

sentences.zh: 彥博再致仕，及甫知河陽，召為太僕卿，權工部侍郎，罷為集賢殿修撰、提舉明道宮。

translations.literal: When Yanbo retired again, Jifu administered Heyang, was summoned as Director of the Imperial Stud, Acting Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, then dismissed as Reviser at the Hall for Assembling the Worthy and intendant of the Mingdao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanbo retired again, Jifu administered Heyang, was summoned as director of the imperial stud and acting vice director of the Ministry of Works, then dismissed as reviser at the Hall for Assembling the Worthy and intendant of the Mingdao Palace.

sentences.zh: 蔡渭、邢恕持及甫私書造梁燾、劉摯之謗，逮詣詔獄，及甫有憾於元祐，從而實之，亦坐奪職。

translations.literal: Cai Wei and Xing Shu took Jifu's private letter to fabricate slander against Liang Tao and Liu Zhi; when brought to the edict prison Jifu, bearing grievance against Yuanyou, followed in substantiating it and also sat stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Wei and Xing Shu used Jifu's private letter to fabricate slander against Liang Tao and Liu Zhi; when brought before the edict prison Jifu, bearing grievance against Yuanyou, followed in substantiating it and was also stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復之，卒。

translations.literal: Before long he was restored, then died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was restored, then died.

sentences.zh: 論曰：國家當隆盛之時，其大臣必有耆艾之福，推其有餘，足芘當世。

translations.literal: The commentary says: When a state is at its height of prosperity, its great ministers must have the blessing of venerable age; extending what they have in surplus is enough to shelter the age.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: When a state is at the height of prosperity, its great ministers enjoy the blessing of venerable age; extending what they have in surplus is enough to shelter the age.

sentences.zh: 富弼再盟契丹，能使南北之民數十年不見兵革。

translations.literal: Fu Bi twice covenanted with the Khitan and was able to keep the peoples of north and south for several decades without seeing arms and armor.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Bi twice made peace with the Khitan and kept the peoples of north and south free of war for decades.

sentences.zh: 仁人之言，其利博哉！

translations.literal: The words of a benevolent man—their benefit is vast!
translations.idiomatic: The words of a benevolent man—their benefit is vast!

sentences.zh: 文彥博立朝端重，顧盼有威，遠人來朝，仰望風采，其德望固足以折衝禦侮於千里之表矣。

translations.literal: Wen Yanbo stood at court with upright weightiness; his gaze had authority; when men from afar came to court they looked up to his bearing—his virtue and standing were truly enough to repel insult at a thousand li's remove.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yanbo stood at court with upright dignity; his gaze commanded authority; when men from afar came to court they looked up to his bearing—his virtue and standing were enough to repel insult a thousand li away.

sentences.zh: 至於公忠直亮，臨事果斷，皆有大臣之風，又皆享高壽於承平之秋。

translations.literal: As for public loyalty, directness, and brightness, and decisive action in affairs—all had the manner of great ministers, and all moreover enjoyed long life in an age of peace.
translations.idiomatic: In public loyalty, directness, and brightness, and in decisive action in affairs, both had the manner of great ministers, and both enjoyed long life in an age of peace.

sentences.zh: 至和以來，建是大計，功成退居，朝野倚重。

translations.literal: From Zhihe onward they established the great design; when the achievement was done they withdrew, and court and countryside relied on their weight.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhihe onward they established the great design; when the work was done they withdrew, and court and countryside relied on their weight.

sentences.zh: 熙、豐而降，弼、彥博相繼衰老，憸人無忌，善類淪胥，而宋業衰矣！

translations.literal: From Xi and Feng downward, Bi and Yanbo in succession grew old; crafty men were without restraint, the good sort were ruined together, and the Song enterprise declined!
translations.idiomatic: From the Xi and Feng reigns downward, Bi and Yanbo in succession grew old; crafty men were without restraint, the good were ruined together, and the Song enterprise declined!

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「番番良士，膂力既愆，我尚有之。」

translations.literal: The Documents says: "Steadfast worthy men—though their strength is spent, I still have them."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says, "Steadfast worthy men—though their strength is spent, I still have them."

sentences.zh: 豈不信然哉！

translations.literal: How can this not be truly so!
translations.idiomatic: How can this not be truly so!
